GPR26 ↔ L-glutamic acid LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE medium confidence ipTM 0.94 · pTM 0.82
Rationale
The fold is confident (ipTM 0.94, iface pLDDT 94.5), but that is the expected result for a small molecule in a GPCR pocket and is not evidence of specificity. ChEMBL records no activity of glutamate at GPR26, while glutamate is measured at ≥76 distinct unrelated targets — a classic promiscuous metabolite that will dock confidently into one more pocket. Note also that all known glutamate GPCRs are class C receptors with an extracellular Venus-flytrap domain, whereas GPR26 is a class A 7TM orphan, so the modeled pocket is not the established glutamate-recognition architecture.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists only 1 disulfide bond and no glycosylation/lipidation features; the single PubMed "PTM" hit is an unrelated behavioural paper. No PTM artifact concern.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
Resolved to CHEMBL575060 (glutamate, SMILES C(CC(=O)O)[C@@H](C(=O)O)N, InChIKey WHUUTDBJXJRKMK-VKHMYHEASA-N). chembl_known_activity at Q8NDV2 (GPR26): 0 activities — no measured affinity at this receptor. chembl_ligand_promiscuity: 462 affinity measurements across ≥76 distinct targets (EAAT1/2, beta-2 adrenergic, D1 dopamine, CYPs, estrogen receptor, bacterial enzymes) — a highly promiscuous small metabolite.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Counter-screen: fold glutamate against 2-3 unrelated class-A GPCRs with the identical protocol — if it scores comparably everywhere, the GPR26 pose carries no information. If pursued, check whether contacts lie in the TM bundle (buried_fraction, pocket topology) and test functionally with a cAMP assay in GPR26-transfected cells, since GPR26 is constitutively Gs-active.

GPR26 ↔ 4-aminobutanoic acid INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE low confidence ipTM 0.92 · pTM 0.82
Rationale
Neither discriminating small-molecule check could be run: resolve_small_molecule returned no ChEMBL id for GABA (PubChem only, three name variants), and both chembl_known_activity and chembl_ligand_promiscuity returned HTTP 500 twice. What remains is a confident fold (ipTM 0.92), which is the expected result for a small metabolite in a GPCR pocket and not evidence of specificity, plus biological plausibility (GPR26 is a brain-enriched orphan Gs-coupled GPCR per UniProt/HPA). If the ChEMBL checks come back empty, the default reading is LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET rather than CONFIRMED_NOVEL.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists no glycosylation or lipidation features for GPR26 (one disulfide bond only). The single pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hit (PMID 21924326) is about the knockout mouse phenotype and CREB phosphorylation, not a GPR26 modification. No PTM artifact concern on the receptor side.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
No ChEMBL result obtained (server errors). UniProt annotates GPR26 as an orphan receptor with no endogenous ligand listed, which is consistent with, but does not establish, novelty. STRING/CellPhoneDB do not index metabolite-receptor pairs and were not queried.

UniProt describes GPR26 as an orphan receptor with constitutive Gs activity and no assigned endogenous ligand. The ChEMBL activity lookup at Q8NDV2 errored, so it is unverified. STRING, CellPhoneDB and pubmed_cooccurrence were not called because they do not index a metabolite partner.

GPR101 ↔ L-glutamic acid LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE medium confidence ipTM 0.89 · pTM 0.63
Rationale
L-glutamic acid resolved only via PubChem (no ChEMBL id returned; ChEMBL API returned 500 on both retries, so no measured activity or promiscuity count could be retrieved), but glutamate is a ubiquitous endogenous metabolite active at dozens of targets (iGluRs, class C mGluRs, transporters) and its well-characterized receptors bind it in a large extracellular Venus-flytrap domain, not the class A transmembrane pocket of GPR101 (UniProt Q96P66, "Orphan receptor", 7 TM, Glycoprotein). The AF3 numbers (ipTM 0.89, iface pLDDT 88, BSA 451 Å2) are exactly the expected result for a tiny zwitterionic metabolite dropped into any GPCR pocket and are not on the same scale as protein-pair confidence, so they add nothing about specificity. Coexpression context is at least coherent (GPR101 is brain/neuron-enriched in HPA; producer gene SLC1A2 is the astrocytic glutamate transporter), which keeps this from being IMPLAUSIBLE.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists 2 Glycosylation sites and 1 disulfide on GPR101 (typical GPCR N-terminal/ECL glycans); pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 1 unrelated hit (GnRH-(1-5)/EGFR transactivation). Not a specific concern for a TM-bundle small-molecule pocket.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)

Follow-up (not yet executed): Retry ChEMBL once the API is up to confirm zero measured activity at Q96P66 and glutamate's target count. The decisive experiment is a counter-screen: fold glutamate against 2-3 unrelated class A GPCRs — if the pose is equally confident everywhere, the signal is pocket-generic. Also inspect whether contacts lie within the TM bundle (orthosteric) rather than on extracellular loops, and validate with a cell-based cAMP/BRET assay for glutamate at GPR101.

Rationale
ChEMBL records no measured activity of T3 (CHEMBL1544) at MRGPRF (Q96AM1), so the pair is not already known, but nothing beyond the confident fold (ipTM 0.89, ligand pLDDT 70.3) supports specificity. The promiscuity lookup failed twice with a server error, so the number of distinct T3 targets is unmeasured here, which is why confidence is low. MRGPRF is an orphan GPCR that UniProt suggests may bind a neuropeptide (a different chemical class), and the listed producer gene DIO3 is, to my knowledge, the deiodinase that inactivates T3 rather than making it, so the production-site link is weak.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: Glycoprotein keyword with 1 annotated glycosylation site (location not checked; on a GPCR this is typically the extracellular N-terminus). pubmed_ptm_glycosylation: 0 hits. There is no evidence that the glycan affects a transmembrane-bundle pocket, so this is not treated as a PTM artifact.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
ChEMBL: no measured activity for T3 at MRGPRF. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not queried because they do not index a metabolite against a receptor. UniProt lists MRGPRF as an orphan receptor ("may bind to a neuropeptide").
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule: CHEMBL1544 (resolved via PubChem), SMILES and InChIKey AUYYCJSJGJYCDS-LBPRGKRZSA-N match the supplied structure. chembl_known_activity at Q96AM1 (target CHEMBL4523903): 0 activities, 0 affinity measurements. chembl_ligand_promiscuity: HTTP 500 on both attempts, so no target count was obtained. From background knowledge, not tool output: T3 is a hormone with established high-affinity targets (thyroid hormone receptors, serum binding proteins, transporters), so it would be expected to dock confidently into other pockets too. Supplied fold metrics: ligand pLDDT 70.3, interface pLDDT 86.6, min separation 3.01 A (no clash), BSA 841 A2. No fold was run here, so there is no ligands block: buried fraction and pocket topology (transmembrane bundle vs loops) are unverified.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Counter-screen: fold T3 against two or three unrelated GPCRs (including other MRGPR family members) and check whether ipTM and ligand pLDDT are equally high; that is the experiment that would establish specificity. 2) Read the ligand pose for MRGPRF-T3: buried fraction and whether contacts are on the transmembrane bundle rather than loops or the cytoplasmic face. 3) Re-run chembl_ligand_promiscuity when ChEMBL is back up. 4) Re-check the producer-gene assignment: DIO1/DIO2 (T4 to T3) are the more appropriate producers than DIO3. 5) If the pose survives the counter-screen, test T3 in an MRGPRF functional assay (beta-arrestin recruitment or Ca2+/cAMP) with reverse T3 and T4 as controls.

GPR12 ↔ L-glutamic acid LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.88 · pTM 0.77
Rationale
Nothing beyond the confident fold (ipTM 0.88) supports glutamate binding GPR12 specifically, and a confident pose is the expected result for a small molecule in a GPCR pocket. UniProt describes GPR12 as constitutively active with putative lipid ligands (sphingosylphosphorylcholine, sphingosine-1-phosphate), a different chemical class from a small polar amino acid, and the supplied p_twoway of 0.055 is not significant. Both ChEMBL checks failed with server errors on two attempts, so novelty and promiscuity are unverified; that is why confidence is low.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists GPR12 as a glycoprotein and palmitoylated lipoprotein (2 glycosylation sites, 1 lipidation site, 2 modified residues, 1 disulfide). The glycosylation sites are probably on the extracellular N-terminus or loops and could affect pocket access, but their position relative to the pose was not checked. The pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits (7) were not informative about GPR12 glycosylation. This is not the main concern for this candidate.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
ChEMBL activity lookup was unavailable (server error), so prior pharmacology for this pair could not be checked. UniProt's function text does not mention glutamate; it names only the lipids SPC and S1P as possible endogenous ligands. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence do not apply to a metabolite partner and were not run.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule returned CHEMBL575060 (via the PubChem fallback), SMILES C(CC(=O)O)[C@@H](C(=O)O)N, InChIKey WHUUTDBJXJRKMK-VKHMYHEASA-N, matching the folded structure. chembl_known_activity (P47775) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity both returned HTTP 500 on two attempts each, so there is NO ChEMBL data: neither absence of measured affinity at GPR12 nor a promiscuity count was established. No fold was re-run, so pocket topology (transmembrane bundle vs loops) is unchecked; supplied metrics are BSA 438 Å2, min separation 3.14 Å, ligand pLDDT 83.8.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Re-run chembl_known_activity (P47775 / CHEMBL575060) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity when ChEMBL is back; a measured affinity would change the verdict to ALREADY_KNOWN. 2) Counter-screen: fold glutamate against two or three unrelated class A GPCRs, with a real metabotropic glutamate receptor as positive control; similar ipTM everywhere would confirm the pocket is non-specific. 3) Inspect the pose for contacts on the transmembrane bundle and compare it with the lipid-binding site in the available GPR12 structure. 4) If the candidate is still pursued, test glutamate in a cAMP assay on GPR12-expressing cells, bearing in mind the receptor's high constitutive Gs activity.

GPR12 ↔ 4-aminobutanoic acid LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE medium confidence ipTM 0.87 · pTM 0.78
Rationale
ChEMBL records no measured activity of GABA (CHEMBL96) at GPR12 (P47775), but GABA has 277 affinity measurements across at least 75 distinct, largely unrelated targets, so a confident fold (ipTM 0.87) into one more pocket is not specific evidence. UniProt gives GPR12's proposed endogenous ligands as the lipids S1P and SPC, a different chemical class from a small zwitterionic amino acid, and the supplied BSA of 386 A2 only shows the molecule is contacted, not that it sits in the orthosteric site. Brain co-expression with the GABA producer GAD2 makes an encounter possible but does not show binding.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists 2 glycosylation sites, 1 lipidation (palmitate) and 2 modified residues on GPR12. For a GPCR these are most likely N-terminal/extracellular glycans and a C-terminal palmitate, which would not obviously occlude a transmembrane-bundle pocket, but site positions were not checked. The PubMed PTM hits were about GPR3, SPC and unrelated proteins, with nothing specific to GPR12 glycosylation. Not treated as the main concern.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
No ChEMBL activity for GABA at GPR12. UniProt describes GPR12 as a constitutively active Gs-coupled orphan receptor with S1P and SPC as possible endogenous lipid ligands; GABA is not mentioned. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not queried because they index protein pairs, not a metabolite against a receptor.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule: 4-aminobutanoic acid = CHEMBL96, SMILES C(CC(=O)O)CN, InChIKey BTCSSZJGUNDROE-UHFFFAOYSA-N (matches the supplied structure). chembl_known_activity at P47775 (CHEMBL5006): 0 activities (first call returned a server error; the retry succeeded). chembl_ligand_promiscuity: 277 affinity measurements at >=75 distinct targets (a floor), including GABA-A receptors, 5-HT3A, dopamine D1, FFAR3, several CYPs, arylsulfatase A and ferritin light chain. Many of these are probably inactive screening records, but the molecule is broadly profiled and not selective.
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here. (1) Counter-screen: fold GABA against two or three unrelated class A GPCRs, plus GPR3 and GPR6 as close paralogs, and compare ligand pLDDT and buried fraction; similar confidence everywhere would confirm non-specificity. (2) Re-fold GPR12 with GABA and read the ligands block: buried_fraction and whether the contacts are on transmembrane segments (the orthosteric lipid pocket) or on loops or the cytoplasmic face. (3) Fold S1P or SPC as a positive-control comparison. (4) If the pose still looks specific, test GABA in a GPR12 cAMP assay; the receptor's high constitutive Gs activity means an inverse-agonist or modulator readout is needed.

Rationale
The confident fold (ipTM 0.87) is the expected result for a flexible lipid in a GPCR pocket and nothing independent supports specificity for GPR50. GPR50 is an orphan melatonin-related receptor, enriched in pituitary lactotrophs and at the plasma membrane, with no lipid ligand in its UniProt function text. Leukotriene D4 resolved only via PubChem with no ChEMBL id, so neither ChEMBL check could be run; novelty and promiscuity are therefore unmeasured, not shown.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt for GPR50 lists no glycosylation or lipidation features, only one disulfide bond. The 4 pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits are functional papers, not PTM reports. There is no receptor-side PTM artifact concern.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
No measured LTD4–GPR50 pharmacology was retrievable (no ChEMBL id). UniProt describes GPR50 as an orphan melatonin-related receptor with scaffold and signalling-modulator roles (TGFBR1, KAT5) and names no small-molecule ligand. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not run, as they index protein pairs rather than a metabolite against a receptor.

Supplied fold metrics: ligand pLDDT 63.1 (only moderate, well below the interface pLDDT of 85.7), min separation 2.59 Å, 224 contacts, BSA 865 Å². No buried fraction or pocket topology was available, so whether the pose sits in the transmembrane bundle is unknown.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Counter-screen: fold LTD4 against two or three unrelated class A GPCRs, plus CYSLTR1 as a positive control. If ipTM is similar everywhere, the GPR50 pose is non-specific. 2) Check the pose's buried fraction and pocket topology to see whether contacts are in the transmembrane bundle or on loops or the long C-terminal tail. 3) Look up LTD4 in ChEMBL by InChIKey to recover the activity and promiscuity records. 4) If the pose survives the counter-screen, test GPR50 in a functional assay (β-arrestin or Ca2+) with LTD4 against CYSLTR1 as control.

GPR15 ↔ prostaglandin D2 LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.86 · pTM 0.78
Rationale
The confident fold (ipTM 0.86) is the expected result for a small lipid in a GPCR pocket and nothing retrieved supports specificity: UniProt gives GPR15's natural ligand as the chemokine-like polypeptide GPR15LG, a different chemical class from a prostanoid, and HPA shows no particular overlap between the producer PTGDS and GPR15's intestine/lymphocyte expression. Both ChEMBL queries (known activity at P49685 and promiscuity) returned HTTP 500 on two attempts each, so neither prior measured affinity nor the molecule's target count could be checked; confidence is low for that reason.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists no glycosylation or lipidation features for GPR15 (one modified residue; Phosphoprotein keyword). PubMed (PMID 33758080) reports tyrosine sulfation and O-glycosylation of GPR15 regulating its interaction with GPR15L; this presumably concerns the extracellular N-terminus and the peptide ligand rather than a small molecule in the transmembrane bundle, so it is not the main concern here.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
ChEMBL activity lookup at GPR15 failed (500 errors), so prior pharmacology for this pair is unchecked. UniProt names GPR15LG (a polypeptide) as the natural ligand and makes no mention of prostanoids; the PTM literature search also surfaced thrombomodulin EGF5 and TRAP-6 as reported GPR15 ligands, all peptides/proteins. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not run, as they do not index a metabolite against a receptor.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule resolved prostaglandin D2 via PubChem to CHEMBL1235252, with SMILES and InChIKey (BHMBVRSPMRCCGG-OUTUXVNYSA-N) matching the supplied structure. chembl_known_activity (P49685) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity both failed with server 500 errors on two attempts each, so there is NO ChEMBL data for this candidate: ALREADY_KNOWN is not excluded and no promiscuity count is available. From the supplied fold metrics only: the ligand's own pLDDT is 62 (modest, above the ~50 unreliability line), interface pLDDT 85.8, min separation 2.52 Å (no obvious clash), buried surface 900 Å2. No pocket topology or buried-fraction readout was available, so whether the pose sits in the transmembrane orthosteric site is unverified.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Re-run chembl_known_activity (P49685 / CHEMBL1235252) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity once ChEMBL is back; a measured affinity would change the verdict to ALREADY_KNOWN. 2) Counter-screen: fold PGD2 against two or three unrelated GPCRs, and against its established receptors as positive controls, to see whether the confidence is specific to GPR15. 3) Inspect the pose for buried fraction and whether contacts fall on transmembrane residues rather than the extracellular N-terminus/loops where GPR15LG binds. 4) If it survives, test PGD2 in a GPR15 Gi/cAMP or beta-arrestin assay with GPR15LG as the positive control.

GPR174 ↔ prostaglandin D2 LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE medium confidence ipTM 0.86 · pTM 0.8
Rationale
GPR174 (UniProt Q9BXC1) is a class-A GPCR whose documented endogenous agonist is lysophosphatidylserine (also CCL21 under testosterone), i.e. a lipid pocket that readily accommodates an amphipathic fatty-acid-like ligand; PGD2 is a prostanoid with its own established receptors (DP1/CRTH2), so a confident AF3 pose (ipTM 0.86, iface pLDDT 82.5) in this lipid-binding TM bundle is the expected result, not evidence of specificity. ChEMBL was unavailable (repeated 500 errors), so neither measured activity at Q9BXC1 nor the molecule's promiscuity count could be retrieved — prostaglandins are nonetheless broadly active lipid mediators. Receptor localization (HPA: plasma membrane, approved) and expression (lymphoid tissue, T/NK/B cells) are compatible with exposure to PGD2, which is abundantly made by mast cells/PTGDS, so the pairing is not implausible — just unproven by this fold.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists 2 glycosylation sites and 1 disulfide; these are extracellular/ECL2 features typical of GPCRs and unlikely to occlude an intra-bundle orthosteric pocket. PubMed PTM search returned only 2 unrelated functional papers.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule: PGD2 = CHEMBL1235252, InChIKey BHMBVRSPMRCCGG-OUTUXVNYSA-N, SMILES matches supplied. chembl_known_activity and chembl_ligand_promiscuity both failed with ChEMBL API 500 errors on two attempts — no measured-affinity or promiscuity data obtained.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Retry ChEMBL for measured PGD2 activity at Q9BXC1 and its target count once the API is back. Experimentally, the decisive test is a counter-screen: fold/assay PGD2 against GPR174 alongside 2-3 unrelated GPCRs, and run a cAMP/TGFalpha-shedding assay comparing PGD2 with lysoPS at GPR174 (with PTGDR/PTGDR2 as controls).

GPR6 ↔ 4-aminobutanoic acid LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.86 · pTM 0.71
Rationale
The fold is confident (ipTM 0.86, ligand pLDDT 76.3), but that is the expected result for a small zwitterionic metabolite in a GPCR pocket and nothing receptor-specific supports it. UniProt describes GPR6 as a constitutively active Gs receptor possibly activated by lipid-derived agonists (oleic acid, sphingosine 1-phosphate), a different chemical class from GABA. The two ChEMBL checks (known activity at GPR6, promiscuity) could NOT be run because the resolver returned no ChEMBL id, so neither novelty nor promiscuity is established; confidence is low for that reason.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites, 1 lipidation (palmitate) and 3 modified residues. Whether any glycosylation site lies near the modeled pocket was not checked. The pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits (8) are generic GPR3/GPR6 expression and signalling papers, not PTM studies. No evidence of a PTM artifact at the pocket.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
No curated pharmacology check was possible (no ChEMBL id). STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not called because they do not index a metabolite against a receptor. The UniProt function text names only lipid-derived candidate agonists for GPR6 and does not mention GABA.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule was tried under three names (4-aminobutanoic acid, GABA, gamma-aminobutyric acid). Each resolved via PubChem only, to SMILES C(CC(=O)O)CN and InChIKey BTCSSZJGUNDROE-UHFFFAOYSA-N, which match the folded structure, but with molecule_chembl_id = null. chembl_known_activity and chembl_ligand_promiscuity were therefore NOT called: I did not substitute a ChEMBL id from memory, since an unverified id could attach another molecule's data to this candidate. Measured affinity at GPR6 (P46095) and the distinct-target count are both unknown, not zero. Not tool-derived: GABA is a major neurotransmitter with well-established receptors and transporters of its own, so a high target count would be expected.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Obtain GABA's ChEMBL id by InChIKey (BTCSSZJGUNDROE-UHFFFAOYSA-N) from ChEMBL directly, then run chembl_known_activity at P46095 and chembl_ligand_promiscuity; a measured affinity would change this to ALREADY_KNOWN. 2) Counter-screen: fold GABA against 2-3 unrelated class A GPCRs, plus GPR3/GPR12 as paralogs, and compare ipTM and ligand pLDDT; similar confidence everywhere confirms non-specificity. 3) Inspect the pose: confirm contacts are on the transmembrane bundle and check buried_fraction; the supplied BSA of 370 Å2 and min separation of 3.49 Å do not by themselves show an orthosteric pose, and the pocket is reported to bind lipids. 4) If still of interest, a cAMP assay of GABA on GPR6-expressing cells, noting that high constitutive activity will complicate the agonist readout.

GPR82 ↔ prostaglandin D2 LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE medium confidence ipTM 0.86 · pTM 0.83
Rationale
ChEMBL records no measured activity of PGD2 (CHEMBL1235252) at GPR82 (Q96P67), so the pair is not already known, but nothing beyond the fold supports it. GPR82 is an orphan GPCR (UniProt: "Orphan receptor") enriched in lymphoid tissue and Kupffer cells, while the listed producer PTGDS is enriched in testis, epididymis, decidua and retinal pigment epithelium, with no overlap. A confident ipTM (0.86) is the expected result for a lipid metabolite in a GPCR pocket, and the ligand's own pLDDT is only moderate (68.7).
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists GPR82 as a glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites; pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 0 hits. The sites were not mapped to the pose, but in a GPCR they are typically on the extracellular N-terminus or loops and unlikely to block a pocket inside the transmembrane bundle. Not treated as the main concern.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
No ChEMBL activity for PGD2 at GPR82, and UniProt lists GPR82 as an orphan receptor with no ligand. STRING, CellPhoneDB and pubmed_cooccurrence were not run because they do not index a metabolite against a receptor.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule returned CHEMBL1235252 via the PubChem fallback, with SMILES and InChIKey (BHMBVRSPMRCCGG-OUTUXVNYSA-N) matching the supplied structure. chembl_known_activity at Q96P67 returned 0 activities. chembl_ligand_promiscuity (500 error on the first call, succeeded on retry) returned 4 affinity measurements at 4 distinct targets, including ALDH1A1 and SLCO2A1. That count is a floor and probably an undercount for this record: it does not show PGD2's cognate receptors PTGDR and PTGDR2, which I know from general pharmacology rather than from a tool result. The low count is therefore not evidence of selectivity.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Counter-screen: fold PGD2 against two or three unrelated GPCRs, and fold GPR82 against other prostanoids (PGE2, PGF2a) and unrelated lipids, to see whether the confidence is specific to this pair. 2) Inspect the pose: confirm the contacts are on transmembrane-bundle residues, check buried fraction (supplied BSA is 942 Å2), and rule out clashes (supplied minimum separation is 2.28 Å). No fold was run here. 3) Check HPGDS expression in Kupffer and lymphoid cells as an alternative PGD2 source. 4) If specificity holds, test in a functional assay (β-arrestin recruitment or cAMP/Gi) for PGD2 at GPR82, with PTGDR and PTGDR2 as positive controls.

UniProt lists GPRC5C as a Glycoprotein with 1 glycosylation site (presumably on the extracellular N-terminus, not checked per-residue) and as a Phosphoprotein with 6 modified residues (likely on the cytoplasmic tail, also not checked). GPR75 ↔ 2-arachidonoylglycerol INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE low confidence ipTM 0.85 · pTM 0.63
Rationale
The two checks that discriminate for a small molecule could not be run: chembl_known_activity (O95800 x CHEMBL122972) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity both returned HTTP 500 on two attempts each, so neither ALREADY_KNOWN nor novelty nor promiscuity is established from tool evidence. What remains is a confident fold (ipTM 0.85), which is the expected result for a metabolite in a GPCR pocket and not evidence of specificity; the supplied p_twoway of 0.056 and ligand pLDDT of 61.7 are unremarkable. Receptor-side evidence is compatible (plasma-membrane GPCR, brain/retina enhanced; UniProt lists CCL5 as activator), so this is not IMPLAUSIBLE, and my lean, if ChEMBL shows no activity at GPR75, is LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET rather than CONFIRMED_NOVEL.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: GPR75 is a glycoprotein with 3 annotated glycosylation sites. Their position relative to the modeled pocket is unknown without a fold; on a GPCR these are typically on the extracellular N-terminus/loops and would be unlikely to block a transmembrane-bundle lipid site, so this is a minor caveat. pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 11 hits, but the titles shown concern 20-HETE/GPR75 signalling, not GPR75 modification.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
ChEMBL lookup for this pair failed (server error), so known pharmacology is unchecked. UniProt's function text names the chemokine CCL5/RANTES as the activator of GPR75. The PubMed hits returned by the PTM search are all about 20-HETE signalling through GPR75 (e.g. PMID 39541047, 35081581, 33011364), i.e. an arachidonate-derived lipid is already the literature's proposed ligand. That makes an eicosanoid-like lipid pocket chemically plausible, but it also means a pocket that accepts 20-HETE would be expected to accept 2-AG in a fold whether or not it binds. STRING, CellPhoneDB and pubmed_cooccurrence are protein-pair tools and were not applicable to a metabolite partner.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule: 2-arachidonoylglycerol = CHEMBL122972, SMILES CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\C/C=C\C/C=C\CCCC(=O)OC(CO)CO, InChIKey RCRCTBLIHCHWDZ-DOFZRALJSA-N (matches the supplied structure). chembl_known_activity at O95800: NOT OBTAINED (ChEMBL API 500 error, tried twice). chembl_ligand_promiscuity: NOT OBTAINED (500 error, tried twice). No measured-affinity count or distinct-target count is available from this run. From general background, not verified here: 2-AG is an endocannabinoid with established activity at CB1/CB2 and several other targets, which would argue for promiscuity, but that is not a tool result. Supplied pose metrics: BSA 875 A2, 293 contacts, min separation 1.97 A (on the tight side), ligand pLDDT 61.7 (modest), interface pLDDT 79.2. No ligands block or pocket topology was available, so whether the pose sits in the transmembrane bundle is unknown.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Re-run chembl_known_activity (O95800, CHEMBL122972) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity (CHEMBL122972) when the ChEMBL API recovers; a measured affinity at GPR75 makes this ALREADY_KNOWN, and a large distinct-target count makes it LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET. 2) Inspect the pose: buried fraction, whether contacts are on transmembrane segments versus loops or cytoplasmic side, and the 1.97 A minimum separation for clashes. 3) Counter-screen: fold 2-AG against two or three unrelated GPCRs, and fold 20-HETE and a decoy lipid against GPR75, to see whether the confidence is specific. 4) Only if those hold up, a wet-lab test (e.g. Gq calcium/IP1 assay in GPR75-expressing cells with 2-AG, with 20-HETE as comparator).

GPR171 ↔ prostaglandin D2 LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.84 · pTM 0.84
Rationale
The confident fold (ipTM 0.84) is the expected result for a small molecule in a GPCR pocket, and nothing retrieved supports specificity for GPR171. UniProt annotates GPR171 as the receptor for the neuropeptide Big LEN, a different chemical class from a prostanoid lipid, and HPA shows no overlap between GPR171 expression (T cells, NK cells, lymphoid tissue) and the PTGDS producer cell types. Both ChEMBL checks failed with HTTP 500 on two attempts each, so neither known activity at this receptor nor the molecule's promiscuity was measured; confidence is low for that reason.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists the Glycoprotein keyword and 1 glycosylation site on GPR171; pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 0 hits. A single N-glycan on a GPCR is typically on the extracellular N-terminus or a loop and is unlikely to occlude a transmembrane-bundle pocket, but its position relative to the modeled pose was not checked. Not treated as the main concern.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
Not established either way. The ChEMBL lookup for PGD2 at GPR171 (O14626) errored twice, so the pair could not be confirmed as novel or already known. UniProt's function text for GPR171 names only Big LEN (a proSAAS-derived peptide) as its ligand and does not mention prostaglandins. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not called because they do not index a metabolite against a receptor.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule returned CHEMBL1235252 (PROSTAGLANDIN D2), InChIKey BHMBVRSPMRCCGG-OUTUXVNYSA-N, matching the supplied InChIKey, so the folded structure is the right molecule. chembl_known_activity (O14626) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity both returned 500 Internal Server Error on two attempts each: NO ChEMBL data was obtained. Whether a measured affinity at GPR171 exists and how many distinct targets PGD2 is active at are therefore unknown from this run; no promiscuity count is reported. Supplied fold metrics: ligand pLDDT 64.6 (moderate, above the ~50 unreliability line), interface pLDDT 85.1, min separation 2.14 A (tight for an un-relaxed pose), BSA 815 A2, p_twoway 0.037. No fold was run here, so pocket topology (transmembrane bundle vs. loops) and buried fraction were not checked.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Re-run chembl_known_activity (O14626 / CHEMBL1235252) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity once ChEMBL is back. A measured affinity would change the verdict to ALREADY_KNOWN, and the target count is needed to make the promiscuity call properly. 2) Counter-screen: fold PGD2 against two or three unrelated GPCRs, plus its cognate receptors PTGDR and PTGDR2 as positive controls, and compare ligand pLDDT, buried fraction and pocket topology. 3) Inspect the existing pose: confirm the contacts lie in the transmembrane bundle and that the 2.14 A minimum separation is not a clash. 4) If it still stands, test PGD2 in a Gi-coupled functional assay (cAMP inhibition or beta-arrestin) on GPR171-expressing cells, with Big LEN as the reference agonist.

P2RY10 ↔ prostaglandin D2 LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.82 · pTM 0.83
Rationale
The fold is confident (ipTM 0.82), but that is the expected result for a lipid-like metabolite in a GPCR pocket and nothing I pulled makes it specific to P2RY10. The ChEMBL checks could not be run: prostaglandin D2 resolved only via PubChem with no ChEMBL id (tried two names), so neither known activity at O00398 nor promiscuity was tested. UniProt lists P2RY10 only as a putative purine receptor, and the supplied ligand pLDDT of 62.4 is modest.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists 3 glycosylation sites and 1 disulfide bond on P2RY10, and the Glycoprotein keyword; pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 0 hits. In a GPCR these sites are typically on the extracellular N-terminus or loops and are unlikely to block a transmembrane pocket, but their position relative to the pose was not checked.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
No measured-affinity lookup was possible because the molecule has no ChEMBL id from the resolver. UniProt function for P2RY10 is "Putative receptor for purines coupled to G proteins", with no prostanoid annotation. STRING and CellPhoneDB do not index metabolite-receptor pairs and were not called.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule ("prostaglandin D2" and "PGD2") returned source=pubchem, molecule_chembl_id=null, with SMILES and InChIKey (BHMBVRSPMRCCGG-OUTUXVNYSA-N) matching the folded structure. Because there is no ChEMBL id, chembl_known_activity and chembl_ligand_promiscuity were NOT run; absence of known activity at P2RY10 and the molecule's target count are both unverified, not negative results. From background knowledge rather than tool output: PGD2 has established receptors of its own (PTGDR/DP1, PTGDR2/CRTH2), and P2RY10 has been reported as a lysophospholipid (lysophosphatidylserine) receptor, so a pocket that accepts an acidic lipid is unsurprising. Supplied fold metrics: ligand pLDDT 62.4, interface pLDDT 82.0, min separation 2.03 Å, BSA 922 Å2. No ligands block or pocket topology was available, so whether the pose sits in the transmembrane orthosteric site is unknown.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Look up PGD2 in ChEMBL directly by InChIKey BHMBVRSPMRCCGG-OUTUXVNYSA-N and run the known-activity (O00398) and promiscuity checks that could not be run here. 2) Counter-screen: fold PGD2 against two or three unrelated GPCRs, with PTGDR/PTGDR2 as positive controls, and fold P2RY10 with lysophosphatidylserine to see whether PGD2 simply occupies the lysophospholipid site. 3) Inspect the pose: buried fraction, whether contacts are on transmembrane helices, and whether the 2.03 Å minimum separation is a clash. 4) If it survives those, test PGD2 on P2RY10-expressing cells in a functional assay (e.g. G-protein signalling or TGFα shedding).

GPR160 ↔ leukotriene D4 LIKELY_PROMISCUOUS_POCKET VALIDATE medium confidence ipTM 0.81 · pTM 0.77
Rationale
The confident fold (ipTM 0.81) has nothing receptor-specific behind it. GPR160 is an orphan plasma-membrane GPCR (UniProt function: "Orphan receptor"), so compartment access is plausible, but leukotriene D4 resolved only via PubChem with no ChEMBL id, so neither measured affinity at GPR160 nor promiscuity could be checked. From background knowledge rather than tool output, LTD4 already has dedicated high-affinity receptors (CYSLTR1/CYSLTR2), and a long flexible amphipathic lipid is the kind of ligand AF3 places confidently in any GPCR bundle; the ligand's own pLDDT is only moderate (62.1).
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists GPR160 as a glycoprotein with 1 glycosylation site, presumably on the extracellular N-terminus or a loop. The PubMed PTM search returned 3 hits, none actually about GPR160 glycosylation. This is unlikely to affect an intra-bundle pocket and is not the main concern.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
No curated pharmacology could be retrieved for this pair because the molecule has no ChEMBL id. UniProt lists GPR160 as an orphan receptor with no ligand. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not queried, as they do not index a metabolite against a receptor.
Small molecule (ChEMBL)
resolve_small_molecule returned a PubChem-only hit (InChIKey YEESKJGWJFYOOK-IJHYULJSSA-N, SMILES matching the folded structure) with molecule_chembl_id = null. chembl_known_activity and chembl_ligand_promiscuity were therefore not run; no measured affinity at GPR160 (Q9UJ42) was confirmed or excluded, and the number of distinct targets is unknown. From background knowledge, LTD4 is the cognate agonist of CYSLTR1/CYSLTR2. Supplied pose metrics: ligand pLDDT 62.1, interface pLDDT 83.5, min separation 2.59 Å, BSA 868 Å2. No fold was run in this triage, so pocket topology (transmembrane vs loop contacts) and buried fraction are unverified.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Counter-screen: fold LTD4 against 2-3 unrelated GPCRs, with CYSLTR1 as a positive control, to see whether ipTM ~0.8 is receptor-specific. 2) Read the pose's ligands block (buried_fraction, pocket topology) to confirm the contacts are on the transmembrane bundle rather than loops or surface. 3) Search ChEMBL by InChIKey, or GtoPdb/BindingDB, for LTD4 target data. 4) If the pose survives, test LTD4 on GPR160-expressing cells (Ca2+, cAMP or beta-arrestin readout) with a CysLT1 antagonist such as montelukast as a control.

IL21R ↔ GPR141 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.7 · pTM 0.54
Rationale
My original verdict was written without a fold. A real AF3 fold has now been run, and it shows the 2101 Å² A-B interface spanning both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible for two intact single-pass or multi-pass membrane proteins, so the predicted contact cannot be physiological. This removes the "unchecked" gap that justified INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Nothing else offsets it: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all found nothing for the pair, IL21R (T/NK cells) and GPR141 (neutrophil progenitors) are enriched in different cell types, and the partner pLDDT of 54.4 is low. The glycosylation concern is now secondary, because the interface fails on topology first.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists 6 glycosylation sites for IL21R and 2 for GPR141. Site positions relative to the interface were not checked. This is secondary to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning IL21R and GPR141 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction, and GPR141 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
IL2RG
Follow-up (not yet executed): No further modeling is needed unless an extracellular-domain-only construct is tested. Even then, the lack of any literature or co-expression support makes it low priority.

FGFR3 ↔ GPR21 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.67 · pTM 0.53
Rationale
The flagged topology violation is a real structural problem that my earlier INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict did not address. The AF3 fold's A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of two membrane proteins. That cannot happen across an intact membrane, so the ipTM of 0.67 reflects a geometrically impossible contact and not a real binding mode. Nothing else supports the pair. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned nothing (known_interaction_strength=none), so no literature trace offsets the structural problem. The HPA check was marked plausible, but GPR21 has only weak blood-vessel expression with no subcellular or single-cell data, and it doesn't clearly overlap FGFR3's brain, skin and esophagus profile. Co-expression therefore adds little. The glycosylation concern is secondary. I am not choosing LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM, because neither protein is a lectin and the topology failure already explains the artifact.
PTM / glycosylation
FGFR3 has 6 glycosylation sites and GPR21 has 2. Interface location is unknown, but the topology violation matters more than glycans.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention FGFR3 and GPR21 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: none (GPR21 is not in its table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel but has no independent support.
Other subunits
FGF1;FGF2
Follow-up (not yet executed): If pursued, re-fold only the FGFR3 extracellular domain with GPR21's extracellular loops and N-terminus, or the two cytoplasmic domains together, so the interface stays on one side of the membrane. Drop the pair if the confidence disappears.

Rationale
The fold check shows the modeled A-B interface includes both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of two single-membrane proteins. That can't happen in an intact membrane, so the large buried surface (BSA 3225 Å2) is probably a bare-sequence artifact and not a real contact. This weakens my earlier LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX call. That call assumed the interface might sit on GRIN1 or GluN2 positions, but the topology problem is a stronger and more direct reason to reject the pose. Other evidence is also weak: ipTM is 0.67, interface pLDDT is about 64, and there are no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hits for the pair. Both proteins being brain plasma-membrane proteins only makes a lateral contact conceivable. It does not support the specific modeled geometry. The glycosylation caveat is untested and doesn't change this.
PTM / glycosylation
GRIN2D has 6 glycosylation sites and GPR6 has 3, plus a palmitoylation site. Whether any lies at the interface was not determined. This is secondary to the topology violation.

IL36RN ↔ GPR87 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.67 · pTM 0.73
Rationale
I'm changing the verdict. My earlier rationale said the fold showed no topology violation. The fold output says the opposite: the IL36RN–GPR87 interface lies entirely on the cytoplasmic face of GPR87. IL36RN is a secreted cytokine and cannot reach the cytoplasm, so the predicted contact is not physically reachable. The missing glycosylation overlap does not help, because the flagged problem is topology, not PTMs. Tissue plausibility from HPA ("plausible") only shows the proteins could be in the same tissue. It does not make a cytoplasmic-face contact possible. There is also no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support, and GPR87's known ligand is a lipid (LPA) while IL36RN's known receptor is IL1RL2. Nothing independent offsets the topology problem, so this looks like an AF3 artifact from folding the two chains without membrane context.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR87 has 3 UniProt glycosylation sites, none at the modeled interface. IL36RN has none. Neither is a lectin. This is not the reason for the downgrade; the topology violation is.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning IL36RN and GPR87 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR87 not in gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No literature trace for the pair.
Other subunits
IL1RL2;IL1RAP;SIGIRR
Follow-up (not yet executed): Only worth revisiting if an extracellular-side contact is predicted, for example by folding IL36RN against the GPR87 N-terminus or extracellular loops only. Otherwise drop the pair.

Rationale
The AF3 fold flagged by the check has two problems. First, the modeled A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, which cannot happen across an intact membrane. That fits my earlier suspicion that the 5561 Å2 buried area was low-confidence disordered sequence draped over the GPCR (pTM 0.43, partner pLDDT 45.5), not a real interface. Second, a glycosylation/lipidation site sits directly on the modeled interface, and AF3 does not represent glycans, so even the extracellular part of the contact is unreliable. The other evidence gives no support to offset this. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all found nothing for the pair. HPA enrichment does not overlap (mesothelial cells for TNFRSF8; mast cells, bone marrow and lymphoid tissue for GPR65). GPR65 is mainly vesicular while TNFRSF8 is at the plasma membrane. With a topologically impossible model and no independent support, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE understated the problem. The confidence is medium rather than high because the topology violation shows the model is wrong, not that the proteins can never interact through a correctly oriented ectodomain contact.
PTM / glycosylation
Both proteins are glycoproteins (TNFRSF8 4 sites, GPR65 3 sites). The fold check shows a glycosylation/lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, and AF3 does not model glycans, so the contact is unreliable.

ROR2 ↔ MRGPRF IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.66 · pTM 0.49
Rationale
I'm changing the verdict from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE. The check is right that HPA gives no protein-level tissue shared by ROR2 and MRGPRF, and neither is secreted, so a direct contact would need both in the same membrane of the same cell. My earlier argument rested on overlapping bone marrow MSC enrichment, which is RNA or single-cell level and weaker than shared protein-level data. Both being plasma-membrane receptors only makes a cis interaction possible in principle. Nothing independent supports it: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were all empty (known_interaction_strength=none), and no AF3 fold was run to give structural support (fold_evidence_status=not_run). The AF3 numbers I cited earlier (ipTM 0.66, interface pLDDT ~60, 6079 Å2 buried) were moderate and looked like non-specific packing without a bilayer. I keep confidence low because the MSC single-cell overlap leaves a small chance of real co-expression.
PTM / glycosylation
ROR2 has 3 glycosylation sites in its ectodomain, and MRGPRF has 1. Whether any lies on the modeled interface is unknown. This is secondary to the co-localization problem.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (MRGPRF not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No prior report, so none of the known-interaction channels offers support.
Other subunits
WNT5A
Follow-up (not yet executed): Only worth revisiting if single-cell or protein-level data show ROR2 and MRGPRF in the same cell type. In that case, re-run AF3 with a membrane-aware setup and with the glycans represented.

GRM8 ↔ MRGPRX2 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.66 · pTM 0.5
Rationale
Both are 7-TM GPCRs with non-overlapping expression: GRM8 is enriched in choroid plexus epithelial cells and cerebral cortex, MRGPRX2 only in mast cells (UniProt: mast cell-specific). A GPCR-GPCR interface this large (BSA 3883 Å2, 1007 contacts) at only moderate interface pLDDT (60.5) is most likely cis packing of the transmembrane bundles, which requires both receptors in the same cell membrane, and nothing here supports that. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all return nothing for the pair, so it is novel but lacks biological support.
PTM / glycosylation
GRM8 is a UniProt Glycoprotein with 5 N-glycosylation sites (presumably in its large extracellular domain) and 8 disulfide bonds. MRGPRX2 has no annotated glycosylation, only 2 disulfide bonds. The PubMed PTM hits for both genes are non-specific (MRGPRX2 mast-cell activation papers; unrelated GRM8 papers). If the modeled interface involves the GRM8 extracellular domain, glycans could interfere, but this is secondary to the expression mismatch.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed co-mentions.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (MRGPRX2 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. Nothing known for this pair.
Other subunits
GRM8 (class C mGluRs function as obligate dimers; this is general knowledge, not from the tools)
Follow-up (not yet executed): Deprioritize. If pursued: (1) inspect whether the interface is transmembrane-helix packing, a common AF3 membrane-protein artifact since no bilayer is modeled, or involves the GRM8 extracellular domain; (2) check for real spatial co-localization of GRM8+ cells with mast cells (e.g. meningeal or choroid plexus mast cells) before any wet-lab test; (3) fold MRGPRX2 against unrelated GPCRs as a specificity control.

  "function": "Mast cell-specific G protein-coupled receptor for basic secretagogues, which regulates mast cell degranulation and itch-related hypersensitivity reactions (PubMed:22069323, PubMed:25517090, PubMed:28288109, PubMed:34789874, PubMed:34789875). HEBP1 ↔ GPR37 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE low confidence ipTM 0.65 · pTM 0.54
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and the AF3 score is moderate (ipTM 0.65, interface pLDDT 68.7). But HEBP1 is a predicted intracellular haem-binding protein and GPR37 is a 7TM GPCR with a glycosylated ectodomain, and I could not determine which face of GPR37 the modelled interface sits on. fold_complex was not available in this session, so no topology check was run. Without it the compartment mismatch is a soft negative, and GPR37's own HPA localisation is rated Uncertain.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR37 is a UniProt Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites, 1 disulfide and Ubl conjugation; N-glycan sites on a GPCR are normally extracellular. If the modelled interface is on the extracellular face, glycans could occlude it and HEBP1 would also be on the wrong side of the membrane. HEBP1 has no annotated PTM features. The PubMed PTM hits for both genes were not informative about the interface.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed co-mentions.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction, and no curated complex for GPR37. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Other subunits
PSAP
Follow-up (not yet executed): Map the AF3 interface residues onto GPR37's UniProt topology (cytoplasmic loops/C-tail versus extracellular N-terminus/loops) and onto its 3 glycosylation sites. A purely cytoplasmic interface would be a plausible novel intracellular docking interaction. An extracellular or mixed cytoplasmic-plus-extracellular interface should be treated as implausible or a glycan artifact unless HEBP1 release is shown. Separately, from background knowledge rather than the tools: an N-terminal HEBP1 peptide (F2L) is reported to be a secreted agonist of the GPCR FPR3, so it may be worth folding the HEBP1 N-terminal peptide alone against GPR37, with the known ligand prosaposin (PSAP) as a positive control. Wet-lab confirmation would be co-IP or BRET in oligodendrocyte-lineage cells. GPR37's 63 HPA-listed interactors suggest a hub, so specificity controls are needed.

GNRH2 ↔ MRGPRX2 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE low confidence ipTM 0.65 · pTM 0.64
Rationale
The flagged problem is real. The AF3 interface for GNRH2-MRGPRX2 includes both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of MRGPRX2, which cannot happen across an intact membrane. The fold therefore gives no support for a binding mode, and I give it no credit toward CONFIRMED_NOVEL or LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX. It is a flaw in this one model, probably from folding the unprocessed GnRH-II precursor, not evidence about the biology, so on its own it does not justify IMPLAUSIBLE. HPA expression is plausible and nothing shows the two proteins cannot meet, but STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned nothing for this pair (strength: none). Plausible expression alone is not interaction evidence. With a discredited structure, no literature or database support, and no evidence against, the pair is neither confirmed nor ruled out.
PTM / glycosylation
No relevant glycosylation for either protein. Mature GnRH-II is a processed, amidated, pyroglutamyl decapeptide, which AF3 did not model. That is another reason to distrust the fold interface.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention GNRH2 and MRGPRX2 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence returned nothing for this pair (strength: none).
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-fold with the mature GnRH-II decapeptide (pyroGlu-His-Trp-Ser-His-Gly-Trp-Tyr-Pro-Gly-NH2) against MRGPRX2. Accept only a pose confined to the extracellular or transmembrane pocket. Alternatively, test experimentally whether GnRH-II activates MRGPRX2, for example in a mast cell degranulation or calcium assay.

GHRL ↔ MRGPRX4 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.65 · pTM 0.66
Rationale
My original rationale said the fold showed no membrane-topology violation. That was wrong. The fold flagged a topology_violation: the whole GHRL–MRGPRX4 interface sits on the cytoplasmic face of MRGPRX4, and ghrelin is a secreted peptide that cannot reach the cytoplasm. The modeled contact is therefore not physiologically possible. The other evidence does not rescue it. HPA says the pair is "plausible" because a secreted hormone and a plasma-membrane GPCR could meet in principle, but that does not make this pose real. Known-interaction strength is none: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all returned nothing. The ipTM of 0.65 is modest and the partner pLDDT of 47.7 is low. The PTM concern (ghrelin octanoylation/amidation, MRGPRX4 glycosylation) was not at the interface, and neither protein is a lectin, so the PTM and glycan-mediated override does not apply. I now treat the prediction as an AF3 artifact, not a novel interaction. Ghrelin's real receptor is GHSR, and MRGPRX4 is a bile-acid/itch receptor. I am not fully certain because ghrelin could in theory contact MRGPRX4's extracellular face, but the modeled interface is not that.
PTM / glycosylation
Ghrelin has octanoylation and amidation. MRGPRX4 has 2 glycosylation sites. None are at the modeled interface, and neither protein is a lectin, so a PTM artifact is not the main problem. The topology violation is.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers for GHRL and MRGPRX4.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no hit (MRGPRX4 is not in its table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No known-interaction support.
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, re-fold with the mature octanoylated ghrelin peptide and check that the contact is on the extracellular or transmembrane-pocket face of MRGPRX4. A cytoplasmic-face pose should be rejected.

CD226 ↔ GPR141 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.64 · pTM 0.54
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and both are plasma-membrane proteins with some bone-marrow overlap, so a cis interaction is topologically possible. However, CD226 carries 8 annotated N-glycosylation sites on its small Ig ectodomain and GPR141 carries 2, none of which AF3 modelled, and a 3242 A2 / 655-contact interface very likely includes that glycosylated surface. I could not verify whether any glycosite sits on the interface because no fold tool was available in this session, so this is an unresolved caveat rather than a demonstrated artifact; the moderate ipTM (0.64) and borderline p_twoway (0.053) do not offset it.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: CD226 is a Glycoprotein with 8 glycosylation sites (plus 3 disulfides and 2 modified residues); GPR141 is a Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM searches (36 hits for CD226, 1 for GPR141) returned nothing specific to these proteins' glycosylation. Eight glycans on CD226's two-Ig-domain ectodomain make it plausible that the modelled contact surface is partly shielded in vivo, but the per-residue position of the sites relative to the interface was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention CD226 and GPR141 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR141 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported. CD226's documented ligands are PVR/CD155 and NECTIN2/CD112; GPR141 is an orphan receptor.
Other subunits
PVR;NECTIN2
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Map the 8 CD226 and 2 GPR141 N-glycosylation sites onto the AF3 interface residues; if any fall on it, re-fold with core glycans attached and see whether the interface survives. 2) Check which topological regions form the interface (ectodomain to extracellular loops, or TM helix to TM bundle); an interface mixing cytoplasmic and extracellular residues would be physically impossible, and TM-TM packing between unrelated membrane proteins is a common AF3 false positive. 3) Confirm same-cell coexpression in single-cell data (NK/T cells, platelets, myeloid progenitors). 4) If the interface survives, test by co-IP or BRET in co-transfected cells, and check whether it competes with PVR/NECTIN2 binding on CD226. PVR and NECTIN2 are listed under other_subunits only as known CD226 ligands for that competition check, not as missing complex members.

SIGLEC1 ↔ GPR141 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM medium confidence ipTM 0.64 · pTM 0.38
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and biologically plausible as a trans contact between two plasma-membrane proteins. However, UniProt describes SIGLEC1 as a lectin whose binding is sialic-acid dependent (14 glycosylation sites), and GPR141 is itself a glycoprotein (2 sites). AF3's bare-sequence interface (ipTM 0.64, interface pLDDT 61.2, pTM 0.38) therefore cannot represent the real glycan-mediated mechanism and may be sterically blocked in vivo.
PTM / glycosylation
SIGLEC1: UniProt keywords Lectin and Glycoprotein, 14 glycosylation sites, and function text stating sialic-acid dependent binding with preference for alpha-2,3-linked sialic acid; its known counter-receptors (e.g. SPN/CD43) are recognised through sialylated glycans. GPR141: Glycoprotein keyword with 2 glycosylation sites, which I assume (not checked per-residue) lie on the extracellular N-terminus or loops. The PubMed PTM searches were mostly non-specific (17 hits for SIGLEC1, including sialylated CD43; 1 unrelated hit for GPR141). Whether any glycosylation site sits on the modeled interface was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning both genes.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR141 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
TYROBP
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run. Map the modeled interface residues onto UniProt topology and glycosylation sites to confirm the contact is extracellular-to-extracellular and whether the SIGLEC1 V-set sialic-acid site or GPR141's N-glycan sites are involved. Re-fold with glycans attached at the GPR141 N-glycosylation sites. Test experimentally with SIGLEC1-Fc binding to GPR141-expressing cells with and without sialidase, and with the sialic-acid-binding-dead SIGLEC1 mutant (R116A in the V-set domain, residue number recalled from the literature, not retrieved here). TYROBP is listed under other subunits only because UniProt mentions it as a SIGLEC1 signalling partner; it is not established as an obligate subunit. With 2014 tokens and pTM 0.38, the long SIGLEC1 Ig-repeat chain is poorly placed overall; a fold restricted to the N-terminal domains would be cleaner.

EFNA3 ↔ GPR21 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.64 · pTM 0.68
Rationale
The fold check found a topology violation. The modeled interface (BSA 5310 Å2, 1124 contacts, partner pLDDT 58) spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of the membrane protein. That cannot happen across an intact membrane, and it confirms my earlier suspicion that the large interface comes from transmembrane or cytoplasmic contacts. My earlier INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict did not account for this. Other evidence also points away from a real interaction. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no prior link. GPR21 is barely expressed (blood vessel 5.1 nTPM, single-cell 'Not detected') and does not overlap with EFNA3's epithelial/keratinocyte profile. EFNA3's known partners are Eph receptors, and GPR21 is an orphan GPCR. Glycosylation on both proteins is a further caveat, but it is secondary. The one remaining route is a genuine extracellular contact between the EFNA3 ectodomain and the GPR21 N-terminus or loops, and nothing supports that. The fold is low-confidence and the prediction is an artifact of unconstrained topology, so I downgrade to IMPLAUSIBLE. Confidence is medium because the absence of data is not proof that the proteins never interact.
PTM / glycosylation
EFNA3 has 3 N-glycosylation sites plus a GPI anchor. GPR21 has 2 glycosylation sites. AF3 did not model the glycans. Site positions relative to the interface were not checked. This is a secondary concern next to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count = 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: none (GPR21 not in the gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. Known_interaction_strength = none, so there is no literature or database support.
Other subunits

CHL1 ↔ GPR12 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.63 · pTM 0.52
Rationale
The real AF3 fold shows the CHL1–GPR12 interface spanning both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible across an intact membrane, so the modeled contact (earlier ipTM 0.63, interface pLDDT 61.6) can't be a real binding mode. This is a concrete structural defect, and my earlier INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict ignored it. On the lectin flag, I still can't re-read GPR12's UniProt FUNCTION text, and what I know of GPR12 (orphan Gs-coupled GPCR) doesn't look like a carbohydrate-binding protein. I am not treating the flag as established, but if it is real it points the same way. AF3 cannot model glycans, so the bare-protein contact would be unreliable whichever residues touch, and CHL1's ectodomain carries 10 glycosylation sites. Both contradictions therefore weaken the prediction. Supporting facts: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all show nothing, and HPA brain co-expression is only plausible, which is not enough to rescue an impossible geometry. I chose IMPLAUSIBLE over LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM because the verified fold failure is solid and the glycan mechanism is not. Confidence is medium because a different, topologically valid CHL1–GPR12 contact is not ruled out.
PTM / glycosylation
CHL1 ectodomain has 10 glycosylation sites and 6 disulfides. GPR12 has 2 N-glycosylation sites and 1 palmitoylation site. The check reports a carbohydrate-binding description in GPR12's UniProt FUNCTION, which I could not verify and which conflicts with its orphan-GPCR biology. If it is real, AF3's glycan-free model could not capture the true binding mode.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 hits for CHL1 with GPR12.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: no hit. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. No known interaction established.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-fold with topology-aware constraints, so that only the CHL1 ectodomain faces GPR12's extracellular N-terminus and loops. Check GPR12's UniProt FUNCTION text manually for the carbohydrate-binding claim. If a glycan-mediated mechanism is plausible, consider modeling glycosylated CHL1.

CATSPER2 ↔ GPR25 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.63 · pTM 0.54
Rationale
CATSPER2 is a pore-forming subunit of the sperm-specific CatSper channel in the sperm flagellum (UniProt; HPA end piece/principal piece), while GPR25 is a lymphocyte chemokine receptor for CXCL17 with HPA enrichment only in stomach, so there is no shared cell type for two integral membrane proteins that would have to meet in the same membrane. No STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed link exists, and the ipTM of 0.63 between a 6-TM channel subunit and a 7-TM GPCR is most likely generic helix-helix packing, with CATSPER2's obligate CatSper partners absent from the model.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists no glycosylation or lipidation features for either protein (GPR25 has one disulfide bond only). The PubMed PTM search returned 2 hits for CATSPER2, neither about its modifications, and 0 for GPR25. There is no PTM basis for an artifact call; the concern is biological context and unmodeled membrane/complex.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for CATSPER2 and GPR25.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction, and GPR25 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported, but that novelty does not outweigh the biological mismatch.
Other subunits
CATSPERB;CATSPERD
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run for this candidate. If it is pursued anyway: (1) inspect the existing model to see whether the interface is purely TM-helix packing; (2) re-fold CATSPER2 with its CatSper partners (CATSPER1/3/4 pore subunits, plus CATSPERB/CATSPERD from CellPhoneDB) to see whether the GPR25 contact surface is already occupied in the native channel; (3) check sperm proteomics for any GPR25 expression. Otherwise deprioritize.

GHRL ↔ MRGPRX1 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.63 · pTM 0.65
Rationale
My original rationale said the fold showed no membrane-topology violation. That was wrong. The fold check flagged the A-B interface as lying entirely on the cytoplasmic face of MRGPRX1. Ghrelin is a secreted peptide and cannot reach the cytoplasm, so the modeled pose is physically impossible. The other evidence does not rescue it. HPA is merely "plausible" (secreted ligand, membrane GPCR). STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed show no prior report (known_interaction_strength=none). ipTM is only moderate (0.63) and partner pLDDT is poor (46.2). Nothing independent supports a real GHRL–MRGPRX1 contact, so I no longer credit this as a confirmed novel interaction. The PTM concern is unchanged. Ser3 octanoylation is real but is not the deciding issue, and neither protein is a lectin.
PTM / glycosylation
GHRL Ser3 octanoylation is real and essential for GHSR, but the fold check found no PTM site at the modeled interface. MRGPRX1's single N-glycan is not at the interface. Neither protein is a lectin. PTM is not the main problem here; the topology violation is.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence count = 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING no association, CellPhoneDB no hit, PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits: no prior known interaction (known_interaction_strength=none). This gives no support for the pair.
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is of interest, re-model ghrelin (including octanoyl-Ser3 and the active N-terminal fragment) against the MRGPRX1 extracellular or orthosteric face, or constrain the docking to that face. Then test it experimentally, for example with a calcium-flux assay.

IFNA7 ↔ GPR151 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.62 · pTM 0.65
Rationale
The fold check shows the IFNA7–GPR151 interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of GPR151. A secreted ligand cannot reach the cytoplasmic face of an intact membrane GPCR, so the moderate ipTM of 0.62 and interface pLDDT of 66.2 probably reflect a bare-sequence packing artifact and not a real contact. My earlier verdict of INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE ignored this. Nothing else offsets it: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no known interaction (strength none), and HPA shows no meaningful co-expression, with both proteins not detected in tissue. IFNA7's known receptors are IFNAR1 and IFNAR2. HPA topology is nominally plausible because one protein is secreted and the other is a membrane protein. However, the fold's topology violation and the lack of any supporting data mean that plausibility is only hypothetical. The two unmodelled glycosylation sites on GPR151 add more doubt about the modeled contact.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR151 has 2 annotated glycosylation sites that AF3 did not model. Their positions were not retrieved. They could be on the extracellular face, but this is secondary to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found, CellPhoneDB no interaction, PubMed 0 hits; known_interaction_strength=none. IFNA7's established receptors are IFNAR1/IFNAR2.
Other subunits
GALR1;GALR2;GALR3
Follow-up (not yet executed): If anyone wants to pursue this, re-fold IFNA7 against only the GPR151 extracellular N-terminus and loops, and check whether the interface stays extracellular-only. Test IFNA7 with IFNAR1 and IFNAR2 as a positive control.

PPIA ↔ GPR3 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE low confidence ipTM 0.62 · pTM 0.61
Rationale
The contradiction is valid. PPIA was folded against 11 receptors and passed the confidence gate for 4 of them (36%), so the moderate AF3 result (ipTM 0.62) for GPR3 mostly reflects PPIA, not GPR3. PPIA is a small, abundant, sticky cyclophilin. The breadth here is not a shared-receptor pattern like a chemokine's, because PPIA has no known promiscuous GPCR-ligand role. Its one established extracellular partner is BSG/CD147, which is not a GPCR. That makes the breadth look like a non-specific fold artifact, and I withdraw CONFIRMED_NOVEL. The other evidence does not rescue specificity. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence are all empty (known_interaction_strength=none), so there is no prior support for this pair. HPA plausibility is only 'plausible', with no subcellular data, so co-localization is not substantiated. The GPR3 glycosylation and palmitoylation sites are unmodeled and unchecked against the interface. I do not call the pair IMPLAUSIBLE, since PPIA is secreted and GPR3 is a surface GPCR. The pair is currently uninformative.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR3 has 1 glycosylation site and 1 palmitoylation site, and PPIA has 1 glycosylation site. AF3 does not model these, and their position relative to the interface was not checked. This matters only if the interface is extracellular.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for PPIA and GPR3.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found; CellPhoneDB no entry (GPR3 absent); PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. No prior evidence of interaction, so this is not ALREADY_KNOWN, but absence also gives no positive support.
Other subunits
BSG
Follow-up (not yet executed): Check PPIA against the full receptor panel and against unrelated negative-control membrane proteins to see whether its confidence is generic. Compare GPR3's ipTM with PPIA to its ipTM with other partners. Check which side of the membrane the interface sits on, and whether the GPR3 glycosylation site is near it. Obtain HPA subcellular data for both proteins.

HCST ↔ GPR65 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.62 · pTM 0.7
Rationale
The fold check found a topology violation. The A-B interface includes both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, which cannot happen across an intact membrane. My earlier LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX verdict ignored this and treated the ipTM of 0.62 as possible TM packing. That reading no longer holds, because the model puts the two proteins in a geometry they can't have in a cell. The weak partner pLDDT (44.8) and the 1.77 Å minimum separation point the same way, toward a non-specific artifact. Nothing else supports the pair: STRING and CellPhoneDB have no record, PubMed co-occurrence is 0, and the known_interaction_strength is none. HPA data on expression overlap and membrane location was marked unknown, so it can't offset the structural problem. HCST (DAP10) has a well-documented partner, KLRK1, which is absent from the model. That makes the predicted GPR65 contact more likely a spurious pairing than a real subcomplex. I am downgrading to IMPLAUSIBLE, with medium confidence because the shared lymphoid expression leaves a small chance of co-localization.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR65: UniProt Glycoprotein keyword with 3 annotated glycosylation sites, plus 2 disulfide bonds; the 6 PubMed hits are functional papers, not PTM-specific. HCST: Glycoprotein and Phosphoprotein keywords, 1 modified residue, 0 PubMed PTM hits. Whether any glycosylation site sits on the modeled interface was not checked, so this is a caveat rather than a finding.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention HCST and GPR65 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found, CellPhoneDB no pair interaction, PubMed co-occurrence 0. No evidence of a known interaction (strength: none).
Other subunits
KLRK1
Follow-up (not yet executed): Optionally re-run AF3 with KLRK1 included and with the membrane topology enforced. Treat any HCST-GPR65 contact as unsupported unless the interface is topologically consistent.

FN1 ↔ GPR82 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.62 · pTM 0.37
Rationale
The fold check shows the predicted FN1–GPR82 interface covers both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of GPR82. FN1 is a secreted protein that can only reach the extracellular face of an intact membrane, so a contact spanning both faces cannot be physical. My original verdict ignored the caveat that no fold tool could check which side of the membrane the interface sat on. That caveat is now resolved against the pair. The remaining points still hold: no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed record of the pair, and the compartment and tissue overlap (liver FN1, Kupffer-cell GPR82) is only plausible, not evidence of binding. The fold is also weak (ipTM 0.62, pTM 0.37, interface pLDDT 62), and FN1 is a promiscuous hub. A topologically impossible pose from a weak fold means the predicted binding mode is likely spurious. I am therefore downgrading from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE. A real extracellular-only FN1–GPR82 contact is not excluded, but nothing here supports one.
PTM / glycosylation
FN1 has 8 glycosylation sites and GPR82 has 2. Neither is shown to lie on the interface. This is a secondary caveat next to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for FN1 and GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR82 not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. GPR82 is an orphan receptor. No prior evidence for the pair.
Other subunits
ITGA5;ITGB1
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair still matters, re-fold only the GPR82 extracellular N-terminus and loops with specific FN1 domains (for example the type III repeats). Check whether the pose stays extracellular-only and confident.

GRIK1 ↔ GPR12 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.61 · pTM 0.47
Rationale
I'm changing the verdict from LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX. (2) The real AF3 fold is the stronger problem. The A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, which is impossible across an intact membrane, so the modeled contact is not a physiologically achievable pose. A glycosylation/lipidation site also sits directly on that interface. This undermines the 'subcomplex' reading, because a real GRIK1-GPR12 contact would have to be a same-side (extracellular-extracellular or cytoplasmic-cytoplasmic) interface, and the fold does not show one. (1) The check says GPR12's UniProt FUNCTION text describes carbohydrate binding. I could not re-read the text and my recollection (lipid-responsive, constitutively Gs-coupled orphan GPCR) disagrees, so I do not rest the verdict on this flag. Even so, the fold-level finding of a glycosylation site on the interface, together with AF3's inability to model glycans, means the bare-protein contact cannot be trusted. Other facts: no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support (known_interaction_strength=none) and HPA plausibility unknown, so there is nothing independent to rescue the modeled interface. I chose ARTIFACT_PTM over IMPLAUSIBLE because both proteins are brain/retina membrane proteins and could plausibly co-localize.
PTM / glycosylation
GRIK1 has 9 glycosylation sites, mostly extracellular. GPR12 has 2 glycosylation sites and 1 palmitoylation site. The fold flagged a glycosylation/lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. The deterministic check also flags GPR12 as glycan-binding per UniProt FUNCTION, which I could not verify and which conflicts with my recollection. AF3 does not model glycans or lipids, so the modeled contact is unreliable either way.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 hits for GRIK1 and GPR12.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR12 not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. Novel, known_interaction_strength=none.
Other subunits
GRIK4;GRIK5
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-model with GRIK1 in its native tetrameric context (with GRIK4/GRIK5) and with glycans represented. Require a topologically consistent interface, either extracellular-extracellular or cytoplasmic-cytoplasmic. Check the GPR12 UniProt FUNCTION text directly. Check for brain-region co-expression of GRIK1 and GPR12.

Rationale
ITGAD is an obligate alpha subunit of the integrin aD/b2 heterodimer (CellPhoneDB: integrin_aDb2_complex with ITGB2), and ITGB2 is absent from the model, so the large modeled surface (BSA 3982 A2) may include the face ITGB2 normally occupies. Both are plasma-membrane proteins co-enriched in lymphoid tissue and T/NK/innate lymphoid cells, so a cis interaction is physically possible, and there is no prior report (STRING none, CellPhoneDB none, PubMed 0). The fold itself is weak support: ipTM 0.61 with interface pLDDT only 58.5, a 1.55 A minimum separation suggesting clashes, and both proteins glycosylated (9 and 3 UniProt sites) with no check of whether those sites sit on the interface.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists ITGAD as a glycoprotein with 9 glycosylation sites and P2RY10 as a glycoprotein with 3. The PubMed PTM search returned nothing relevant (1 unrelated hit for ITGAD, 0 for P2RY10). If the interface involves the ITGAD ectodomain or the P2RY10 N-terminus/extracellular loops, unmodeled glycans could occlude it; site positions relative to the interface were not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for ITGAD and P2RY10.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction (P2RY10 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
ITGB2

Inspect the interface topology for any contact mixing extracellular and cytoplasmic residues, and check whether the N-glycosylation sites of either protein land on the interface. Resolve the 1.55 A clash signal by relaxing the model. If the interface survives, test by co-IP or proximity ligation in T/NK cells.
