ITGB7 ↔ P2RY8 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.61 · pTM 0.6
Rationale
The real AF3 fold shows the ITGB7–P2RY8 interface (BSA 2138 Å2, ipTM 0.61, interface pLDDT 69) spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible across an intact membrane, so the modelled contact is a prediction artifact and not a real binding mode. My earlier LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX verdict was wrong to treat the large interface as a possible alpha-chain-site or TM contact without checking topology. Missing ITGA4/ITGAE can't rescue a pose that breaks membrane topology. Other evidence is weak: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no link for this pair, so there is no known-interaction support. HPA co-expression in lymphoid tissue is only a plausibility argument. Glycosylation (ITGB7 8 sites, P2RY8 2 sites) is an unchecked extra caveat. Together these leave no credible support for a direct interaction, so I'm moving to IMPLAUSIBLE at medium confidence. Co-expression alone doesn't override a topologically impossible fold.
PTM / glycosylation
ITGB7 has 8 ectodomain glycosylation sites and P2RY8 has 2. Glycans were not checked against the interface and are secondary to the topology failure.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for ITGB7 and P2RY8.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction (P2RY8 not in gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel in the literature but has no supporting evidence.
Other subunits
ITGA4;ITGAE
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, re-model ITGB7 with ITGA4 (or ITGAE) and P2RY8 as a trimer. Then check whether any contact is topologically consistent, for example restricted to the extracellular or transmembrane region on the same side of the membrane.

SEMA4C ↔ GPR37 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.6 · pTM 0.61
Rationale
The flagged contradiction holds up. HPA shows no shared protein-level tissue for SEMA4C and GPR37, and neither protein is secreted, so a direct contact would need both to sit in the same place. My original argument for a cis or trans ectodomain contact rested on a general brain-relevance claim and on UniProt membrane annotations. Neither is concrete co-localization data. SEMA4C's low tissue specificity does not show it is present where GPR37 is, in oligodendrocytes. The pair has no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support, and each protein already has its own known partners (PLXNB2 for SEMA4C; prosaposin, osteocalcin and neuroprotectin D1 for GPR37). No real fold was analysed (fold_evidence_status=not_run). The moderate ipTM of about 0.6 therefore can't offset the lack of co-expression, and both ectodomains are N-glycosylated, which AF3 does not model. I'm lowering the verdict from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE with low confidence. Brain RNA-level overlap or a cell-type-specific contact could still exist, but the data I have don't show one.
PTM / glycosylation
SEMA4C has 6 and GPR37 has 3 UniProt N-glycosylation sites on the extracellular side. AF3 does not model these glycans, and no site-to-interface check was done. This is a secondary caveat that adds to the doubt about the modeled contact.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning SEMA4C and GPR37 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. known_interaction_strength=none, so the pair is not already known, but the absence of prior evidence also gives no support for a real interaction.
Other subunits
PLXNB2
Follow-up (not yet executed): Look for single-cell or RNA-level evidence that SEMA4C and GPR37 are co-expressed in the same brain cell type, such as oligodendrocyte lineage cells. Only if co-expression is shown, run a real AF3 fold, check glycan sites against the interface, and consider PLXNB2 as an additional subunit.

TREM2 ↔ GPR82 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.59 · pTM 0.6
Rationale
The fold check shows the TREM2–GPR82 interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible across an intact membrane, so the modeled contact cannot be a real binding mode, and my earlier LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX verdict was wrong to ignore it. The moderate AF3 scores (ipTM 0.59, interface pLDDT 66, partner pLDDT 59) do not offset this. HPA expression and co-localization in tissue-resident macrophages only show the two could meet, and there is no known-interaction evidence (STRING none, CellPhoneDB none, PubMed 0 hits). The TYROBP absence and the glycosylation caveat are secondary. The modeled pose is geometrically invalid, and nothing independent supports a direct TREM2–GPR82 interaction.
PTM / glycosylation
TREM2 has 2 glycosylation sites in its extracellular Ig domain, and GPR82 has 2 glycosylation sites. Whether any lie on the interface is unknown. This is secondary to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-mention count is 0 for TREM2 and GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction, and GPR82 is absent from its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is not previously known.
Other subunits
TYROBP
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, re-fold TREM2 with TYROBP and GPR82 and check that any predicted contact is limited to extracellular or transmembrane segments on the same side of the membrane.

CEACAM1 ↔ MRGPRX3 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.59 · pTM 0.56
Rationale
No prior evidence links this pair (STRING and CellPhoneDB not found, 0 PubMed co-mentions), so it is novel, and both are plasma-membrane proteins per UniProt. However, CEACAM1's ectodomain carries 20 annotated N-glycosylation sites that AF3's bare-sequence model omits, and the modeled interface is very large (BSA 3024 Å2, 524 contacts) for a small orphan GPCR, at only moderate confidence (ipTM 0.59, interface pLDDT 69.4). Whether glycans actually sit on the modeled interface was not checked, and expression overlap is weak, so this is a caveat-driven call rather than a demonstrated artifact.
PTM / glycosylation
CEACAM1: UniProt keyword Glycoprotein with 20 Glycosylation features, plus Phosphoprotein; PubMed returns 112 PTM/glycosylation hits, including a paper on N-glycan conformations at the surface of the CEACAM1 Ig1 domain. This is plausibly relevant because any contact with a GPCR's extracellular face would use the glycosylated Ig ectodomain. MRGPRX3: no Glycosylation or Lipidation features in UniProt and 0 PubMed PTM hits. Whether specific glycan sites lie on the modeled interface was not determined.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning CEACAM1 and MRGPRX3 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found (MRGPRX3 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. Nothing indicates this pair is already known.
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run for this triage (the fold tool was not available in this session). Next steps: (1) map the modeled interface residues against CEACAM1's 20 N-glycosylation sites and against UniProt topology for both proteins, to rule out an interface that mixes cytoplasmic and extracellular residues or sits on the lipid-facing TM surface of MRGPRX3; (2) re-fold with core N-glycans attached at the CEACAM1 sites to see whether the interface survives; (3) check co-expression in the relevant cell types (e.g. DRG sensory neurons for MRGPRX3 versus epithelial or neutrophil CEACAM1) before any wet-lab binding assay. CellPhoneDB does not cover MRGPRX3 and CORUM was not available, so the absence of complex partners is not conclusive.

IL2 ↔ GPR171 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.58 · pTM 0.7
Rationale
The fold check shows the predicted IL2–GPR171 interface lies entirely on GPR171's cytoplasmic face. IL2 is a secreted cytokine and never reaches the cytoplasm, so this pose is topologically impossible. My earlier CONFIRMED_NOVEL verdict relied on the general fact that IL2 is extracellular and GPR171 is a surface receptor. That argument holds only if the contact is on the extracellular side, and the fold shows it is not. The other evidence doesn't rescue the pair. Known-interaction strength is none (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed trace). GPR171's real ligand is the small peptide BigLEN, and IL2 already has its canonical IL2RA/IL2RB/IL2RG receptors. The modest ipTM of 0.58 is likely an artifact of the intracellular-face contact. HPA shows co-expression in T cells, which makes the pair plausible in principle but doesn't change the fact that the modeled contact is impossible.
PTM / glycosylation
Each protein has one annotated glycosylation site, but no position was checked against the interface. This is secondary to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning IL2 and GPR171 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: none. CellPhoneDB: none (GPR171 not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair has no prior literature support.

  "function": "Cytokine produced by activated CD4-positive helper T-cells and to a lesser extend activated CD8-positive T-cells and natural killer (NK) cells that plays pivotal roles in the immune response and tolerance (PubMed:6438535). This process leads to activation of several pathways including STAT, phosphoinositide-3-kinase/PI3K and mitogen-activated protein kinase/MAPK pathways (PubMed:25142963). Functions as a T-cell growth factor and can increase NK-cell cytolytic activity as well (PubMed:6608729). VCAM1 ↔ GPR171 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.58 · pTM 0.48
Rationale
The topology_violation contradiction is valid, and I no longer think CONFIRMED_NOVEL is right. The real AF3 fold's interface includes both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That can't happen across an intact membrane, so the modeled pose is not a physical binding mode. The other evidence doesn't rescue it. No STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed record exists for the pair (known_interaction_strength = none). HPA plausibility (shared lymphoid expression and surface localization) only shows the proteins could meet, not that they bind. The weak metrics already noted (ipTM 0.58, interface pLDDT 69, 1.15 Å minimum separation suggesting clashes) fit a spurious pose. GPR171's known ligand is a short neuropeptide, and VCAM1's known partners are integrins. I'm rating the interaction implausible as modeled. The medium confidence reflects that a legitimate extracellular VCAM1–GPR171 contact hasn't been tested and is not strictly excluded.
PTM / glycosylation
VCAM1 has 6 extracellular N-glycosylation sites and GPR171 has 1. AF3 does not model glycans, but this is secondary to the topology problem.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention VCAM1 and GPR171 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found; CellPhoneDB no match (GPR171 not in table, uninformative); PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. known_interaction_strength=none.
Other subunits

IL12RB1 ↔ GPR174 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.58 · pTM 0.5
Rationale
The fold check shows two problems that I did not account for in the original CONFIRMED_NOVEL call. (1) The A-B interface includes both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of two single-pass or multi-pass membrane proteins. That cannot happen across an intact membrane, so the ipTM of 0.58 is not credible as a real contact. (2) A glycosylation or lipidation site lies directly on the modeled interface. AF3 does not represent that modification, so even the part of the contact that looks plausible could be a bare-sequence artifact. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed still give no prior evidence for this pair. The lymphoid co-expression I relied on only shows the two proteins could be on the same cell. It does not show a specific interaction, and it does not fix the topology problem. The pair is therefore implausible as modeled, not a confirmed novel interaction. A topologically valid re-fold could revisit this, for example extracellular-domain-only constructs.
PTM / glycosylation
The fold flags a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. IL12RB1 has 6 annotated glycosylation sites and GPR174 has 2. AF3 does not model these, so the contact is unreliable. Neither protein is a lectin.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 hits for IL12RB1 and GPR174.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING no association; CellPhoneDB no curated interaction (GPR174 not in its table); PubMed co-occurrence 0. No known interaction, but that absence does not offset the structural problem.
Other subunits
IL12RB2;IL23R
Follow-up (not yet executed): If pursued, re-fold with extracellular domains only, or with IL12RB2 or IL23R included, and check that the interface is on one side of the membrane and avoids glycosylated residues.

  "protein_name": "Probable G protein-coupled receptor 174",
  "function": "G protein-coupled receptor of lysophosphatidylserine (LysoPS) that plays different roles in immune response (PubMed:36823105). Plays a negative role in regulatory T-cell accumulation and homeostasis. Under inflammatory conditions where LysoPS production increases, contributes to the down-regulation of regulatory T-cell activity to favor effector response. Mediates the suppression of IL-2 production in activated T-lymphocytes leading to inhibition of growth, proliferation and differentiation of T-cells. Mechanistically, acts via G(s)-containing heterotrimeric G proteins to trigger elevated cyclic AMP levels and protein kinase A/PKA activity, which may in turn act to antagonize proximal TCR signaling. Rationale
The fold check shows the predicted CFC1–GPR33 interface covers both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of GPR33. That cannot happen across an intact membrane, because CFC1 is secreted or GPI-anchored and sits on the outside. The AF3 pose is therefore not a physically realisable contact, and the borderline ipTM of 0.58 and partner pLDDT of 42.1 do not offset this. Nothing else supports the pair: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed found no trace, and HPA shows GPR33 RNA as not detected in any tissue. The general topology is still permissible, since a secreted ligand could in principle engage the extracellular face of a GPCR. I therefore move from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE for this modeled interaction, with medium confidence because a true extracellular-only contact has not been tested. Glycosylation (CFC1 one site plus a GPI anchor; GPR33 four sites) was not modeled and is a secondary caveat.
PTM / glycosylation
CFC1 has 1 glycosylation site and a GPI anchor; GPR33 has 4 glycosylation sites. These were not modeled by AF3, and whether they lie on the interface was not checked. This is a secondary caveat.

PLXND1 ↔ GPR4 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.58 · pTM 0.48
Rationale
The fold check flagged a topology violation. The modeled PLXND1–GPR4 interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, which can't happen across an intact membrane. That undermines the modeled pose, and my earlier "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE" verdict did not acknowledge it. The flag also says a glycosylation or lipidation site sits directly on the interface. AF3 modeled bare sequence, so the contact may be an artifact of missing glycans. The moderate ipTM (0.58), low interface pLDDT (62.7) and a 1.79 Å minimum separation that suggests clashes all fit a spurious, physically impossible pose. Nothing else supports the pair. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no known interaction, and HPA gave no usable co-expression or localization. I therefore see no independent evidence to offset the topology problem, and I now rate the predicted interface as implausible. I rate confidence medium rather than high because a cis interaction between two membrane receptors is still possible in principle, and the data are sparse rather than contradictory.
PTM / glycosylation
PLXND1 has 18 annotated glycosylation sites and GPR4 has 2. The fold check says a glycosylation or lipidation site lies directly on the modeled interface. AF3 does not represent glycans, so the contact is unreliable.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning PLXND1 and GPR4 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR4 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel but has no literature support.

The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit), brain co-expression is plausible, and both proteins are membrane proteins that could meet at the cell surface or in endosomes. However, UniProt lists 27 glycosylation sites on SORL1 and 3 on GPR52, so a very large modeled interface (BSA ~4389 Å2, 810 contacts) at only borderline confidence (ipTM 0.58, interface pLDDT 61) could plausibly be occluded by glycans AF3 did not model. Whether any glycan site actually sits on the interface was not checked, so this is a caveat-driven call, not a demonstrated artifact.

UniProt: SORL1 is a Glycoprotein with 27 annotated glycosylation sites and 39 disulfide bonds, on its large ectodomain; GPR52 is a Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites. PubMed returned a 2025 Nat Chem Biol paper titled "Post-translational modifications orchestrate the intrinsic signaling bias of GPR52"; the SORL1 PTM search hits were mostly not about glycosylation. The glycan density makes interference with a large ectodomain interface plausible, but per-residue overlap with the modeled interface was not verified.

STRING / CellPhoneDB

If the interface survives, test by co-IP or proximity labelling in striatal neurons, and check whether SORL1 alters GPR52 surface levels or trafficking, consistent with its sorting-receptor role.

input: {"gene": "SORL1"}
{
  "gene": "SORL1",
  "accession": "Q92673",
  "protein_name": "Sortilin-related receptor",
  "function": "Sorting receptor that directs several proteins to their correct location within the cell (Probable). Along with AP-1 complex, involved Golgi apparatus - endosome sorting (PubMed:17646382). Sorting receptor for APP, regulating its intracellular trafficking and processing into amyloidogenic-beta peptides. Retains APP in the trans-Golgi network, hence preventing its transit through late endosomes where amyloid beta peptides Abeta40 and Abeta42 are generated (PubMed:16174740, PubMed:16407538, PubMed:17855360, PubMed:24523320). May also sort newly produced amyloid-beta peptides to lysosomes for catabolism (PubMed:24523320). Does not affect APP trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi compartments (PubMed:17855360). Sorting receptor for the BDNF receptor NTRK2/TRKB that facilitates NTRK2 trafficking between synaptic plasma membranes, postsynaptic densities and cell soma, hence positively regulates BDNF signaling by controlling the intracellular location of its receptor (PubMed:23977241). Sorting receptor for GDNF that promotes GDNF regulated, but not constitutive secretion (PubMed:21994944). Sorting receptor for the GDNF-GFRA1 complex, directing it from the cell surface to endosomes. GDNF is then targeted to lysosomes and degraded, while its receptor GFRA1 recycles back to the cell membrane, resulting in a GDNF clearance pathway. The SORL1-GFRA1 complex further targets RET for endocytosis, but not for degradation, affecting GDNF-induced neurotrophic activities (PubMed:23333276). Sorting receptor for ERBB2/HER2. Regulates ERBB2 subcellular distribution by promoting its recycling after internalization from endosomes back to the plasma membrane, hence stimulating phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-dependent ERBB2 signaling. In ERBB2-dependent cancer cells, promotes cell proliferation (PubMed:31138794). Sorting receptor for lipoprotein lipase LPL. Promotes LPL localization to endosomes and later to the lysosomes, leading to degradation of newly synthesized LPL (PubMed:21385844). Potential sorting receptor for APOA5, inducing APOA5 internalization to early endosomes, then to late endosomes, wherefrom a portion is sent to lysosomes and degradation, another portion is sorted to the trans-Golgi network (PubMed:18603531). Sorting receptor for the insulin receptor INSR. Promotes recycling of internalized INSR via the Golgi apparatus back to the cell surface, thereby preventing lysosomal INSR catabolism, increasing INSR cell surface expression and strengthening insulin signal reception in adipose tissue. Does not affect INSR internalization (PubMed:27322061). Plays a role in renal ion homeostasis, controlling the phospho-regulation of SLC12A1/NKCC2 by STK39/SPAK kinase and PPP3CB/calcineurin A beta phosphatase, possibly through intracellular sorting of STK39 and PPP3CB (By similarity). Stimulates, via the N-terminal ectodomain, the proliferation and migration of smooth muscle cells, possibly by increasing cell surface expression of the urokinase receptor uPAR/PLAUR. This may promote extracellular matrix proteolysis and hence facilitate cell migration (PubMed:14764453). By acting on the migration of intimal smooth muscle cells, may accelerate intimal thickening following vascular injury (PubMed:14764453). Promotes adhesion of monocytes (PubMed:23486467). Stimulates proliferation and migration of monocytes/macrophages (By similarity). Through its action on intimal smooth muscle cells and macrophages, may accelerate intimal thickening and macrophage foam cell formation in the process of atherosclerosis (By similarity). Regulates hypoxia-enhanced adhesion of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells to the bone marrow stromal cells via a PLAUR-mediated pathway. This function is mediated by the N-terminal ectodomain (PubMed:23486467). Metabolic regulator, which functions to maintain the adequate balance between lipid storage and oxidation in response to changing environmental conditions, such as temperature and diet. The N-terminal ectodomain negatively regulates adipose tissue energy expenditure, acting through the inhibition the BMP/Smad pathway (By similarity). Sorting receptor that may regulate signaling by the heterodimeric neurotrophic cytokine CLCF1-CRLF1 bound to the CNTFR receptor by promoting the endocytosis of the tripartite complex CLCF1-CRLF1-CNTFR and lysosomal degradation (PubMed:26858303). May regulate IL6 signaling, decreasing cis signaling, possibly by interfering with IL6-binding to membrane-bound IL6R, while up-regulating trans signaling via soluble IL6R (PubMed:28265003)",

GP1BB ↔ GPR63 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.58 · pTM 0.59
Rationale
The fold check shows the GP1BB–GPR63 interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible across an intact membrane, and my earlier LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX verdict ignored it. The moderate ipTM of 0.58 is therefore best read as a bare-sequence artifact, not a real contact. Nothing else offsets this. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all give no prior evidence for the pair, so known_interaction_strength is none. The shared choroid plexus expression is only weak co-localization, and HPA plausibility is unknown. The GP1BA/Ib-IX complex argument no longer matters, because the modeled interface itself cannot form in vivo. I am moving to IMPLAUSIBLE at medium confidence, because the check rests on a single fold and does not rule out an interaction through some other, topologically valid interface.
PTM / glycosylation
GP1BB has 1 glycosylation site and GPR63 has 3. Whether any lies on the interface is unchecked. This is secondary to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-mention count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found; CellPhoneDB no interaction (GPR63 not in gene table); PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. No known interaction (strength none).

LAIR1 ↔ GPR65 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.58 · pTM 0.55
Rationale
The fold check shows the modeled A-B interface covers both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That cannot happen across an intact membrane, so the 4476 Å2 interface is almost certainly bilayer-free packing of the LAIR1 TM helix against the GPR65 bundle, not a real contact. The check also found a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the interface. My original rationale could only list glycosylation as an unchecked caveat, and the check now shows it applies here. AF3 models bare protein, so this contact is even less trustworthy. The marginal ipTM of 0.58 and the partner pLDDT of 53.5 fit this reading. The lack of any STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed record (known_interaction_strength=none) still means the pair is not known. But an absence of prior evidence does not support a novel claim when the only positive evidence is a topologically impossible model. The overlapping immune expression only shows the proteins could share a membrane. It does not show they interact. I am downgrading from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE, at medium confidence because the topology call comes from an automated annotation.
PTM / glycosylation
LAIR1 has 1 glycosylation site and GPR65 has 3. The fold check places a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, so AF3's bare-sequence model likely misrepresents the contact. Neither protein is a lectin.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for LAIR1 + GPR65.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found, CellPhoneDB no match (GPR65 not in the gene table), PubMed co-occurrence 0. The pair is not known, but this does not support novelty given the structural problem.
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, test an ectodomain-only construct of LAIR1 against the extracellular regions of GPR65. Otherwise test it experimentally, for example by co-IP or proximity ligation in lymphocytes.

Plays a role in immune response by maintaining lysosome function and regulating T-cell metabolism (PubMed:27287411). Acts as a regulator of inflammation by mediating pH-sensing of extracellular acidification which takes place in inflamed tissues: activation regulates endo-lysosomal function of immune cells and T-cell metabolism (By similarity). ITGAM ↔ GPR82 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.58 · pTM 0.48
Rationale
The flagged topology violation changes my view. The modeled ITGAM–GPR82 interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, which is impossible across an intact plasma membrane. The 2627 Å2 contact is therefore most likely a bare-sequence artifact and not a real cis interaction. A glycosylation or lipidation site also sits directly on the modeled interface. AF3 does not represent glycans, so the contact surface may be occluded or altered in vivo, and this further weakens the pose. I had originally framed the problem as a missing ITGB2 subunit, which gave LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX. That no longer fits, because adding ITGB2 would not fix a pose that crosses the membrane. The other evidence is also weak: STRING and CellPhoneDB have no hit, there are 0 PubMed co-mentions, and the fold is borderline (ipTM 0.58, interface pLDDT 64, clashes at 1.53 Å). Both proteins being myeloid plasma-membrane proteins makes co-localization conceivable, but nothing substantiates it, and the HPA plausibility result is unknown. I rate this IMPLAUSIBLE at medium confidence. A real cis association cannot be fully excluded, but this model does not support one.
PTM / glycosylation
ITGAM has 19 annotated glycosylation sites and GPR82 has 2. The structural check found a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. AF3 did not model glycans, so the contact is unreliable.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention ITGAM and GPR82 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR82 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is not known in the literature.
Other subunits
ITGB2

Rationale
No prior evidence for this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed 0 hits), so it is novel, but the model is unlikely to be trustworthy. UniProt describes CD22 as a siglec whose binding to surface partners is through alpha2,6-sialic acid glycans, and its ectodomain carries 11 annotated glycosylation sites, none of which AF3's bare-sequence fold represents. The fold itself is marginal (ipTM 0.57, interface pLDDT 60, minimum separation 1.64 Å with 1242 contacts and 4273 Å2 buried), which looks more like an over-packed or clashing interface than a clean one.
PTM / glycosylation
CD22 (UniProt P20273): keywords Glycoprotein and Lectin, 11 glycosylation sites, and a function text stating it binds alpha2,6-linked sialic acid on surface molecules in cis and trans. The 171 PubMed hits include work on CD22 cis-ligands. GPR25 (O00155): no annotated glycosylation sites and 0 PubMed PTM hits, so a genuine sialoglycan-mediated CD22–GPR25 contact is not supported either. Whether CD22 glycan sites sit on the modeled interface was not tested per residue.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction; GPR25 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0. The pair is novel; GPR25's only documented ligand is CXCL17.
Other subunits
PTPRC;BCR (IgM/CD79A/CD79B)
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run for this triage. Inspect the AF3 model for (a) clashes, given the 1.64 Å minimum separation, (b) whether the interface mixes extracellular and cytoplasmic residues, and (c) whether CD22 N-glycosylation sites lie on the interface. If the interface is ectodomain-to-ectodomain, re-fold with CD22 glycans attached. If it is the CD22 cytoplasmic ITIM tail against GPR25 intracellular loops, treat it as likely low-specificity. Before any wet-lab work, confirm that GPR25 and CD22 are expressed in the same or adjacent lymphocyte populations.

CD244 ↔ GPR34 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.57 · pTM 0.48
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and both are cell-surface immune proteins, so contact is physically possible. But the fold is marginal (ipTM 0.57, partner pLDDT 58.1), and UniProt lists 8 N-glycosylation sites on CD244 and 5 on GPR34 that AF3 did not model. GPR34's documented ligand is a lipid (lysophosphatidylserine) and CD244's is CD48, so nothing supports a specific protein-protein interface here. No fold was run in this session, so whether any glycan site actually sits on the modeled interface is unverified; the verdict rests on the density of glycosylation, not on a confirmed site.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: CD244 carries the Glycoprotein keyword with 8 glycosylation sites (plus Phosphoprotein, relevant only to its cytoplasmic tail motifs); GPR34 carries Glycoprotein with 5 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM searches (28 hits for CD244, 8 for GPR34) returned mostly general signalling papers and nothing site-specific. The fold also flags a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the interface. Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and biologically compatible: both are brain-expressed plasma-membrane proteins per HPA and UniProt. However, UniProt annotates 9 glycosylation sites on LRRC4B (an LRR/Ig synaptic adhesion protein) and 3 on GPR6, and AF3 modelled neither; the fold is also borderline (ipTM 0.57, partner pLDDT 62.6) with a very large interface (BSA 4891 Å2, 810 contacts) for a GPCR with little exposed extracellular surface. Whether any glycan site actually lies on the modelled interface was not checked, so the artifact call is a suspicion, not a demonstrated result.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: LRRC4B is a Glycoprotein with 9 annotated glycosylation sites, which for an LRR/Ig adhesion protein would be on the ectodomain (the only region that could contact GPR6's extracellular face). GPR6 is a Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites and a Lipoprotein with 1 palmitoylation site. The PubMed PTM search gave 0 hits for LRRC4B and 8 non-specific hits for GPR6 (general GPCR signalling and transcriptomics papers, not PTM studies). No per-residue check was done, so it is unknown whether any glycan site is at the modelled interface.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for LRRC4B + GPR6.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR6 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Other subunits
PTPRF
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Map the 9 LRRC4B and 3 GPR6 N-glycosylation sites onto the modelled interface residues; if any are there, re-fold with the glycans attached. 2) Check the interface topology in the 3D model: a 4891 Å2 interface on a GPCR may involve transmembrane or cytoplasmic residues contacting the LRRC4B ectodomain, which would be physically impossible. 3) LRRC4B's known trans-synaptic partner is PTPRF (UniProt function text, by similarity); consider whether GPR6 would compete with it for the LRR surface. 4) If the interface survives these checks, test by co-immunoprecipitation or a cell-surface binding assay in neurons or HEK cells.

PLXNA4 ↔ GPR6 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.57 · pTM 0.46
Rationale
I'm changing the verdict from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. The real AF3 fold shows the PLXNA4–GPR6 interface spanning both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible for two intact membrane proteins, because one contact surface can't lie on both sides of a bilayer. It fits the weak scores (ipTM 0.57, interface pLDDT 55.5, min PAE 8.26 Å) and the very large, probably nonspecific interface (BSA 4175 Å2). A glycosylation/lipidation site also sits directly on the modeled interface. AF3 omits glycans and palmitate, so the contact could be an artifact of the bare-sequence model. This second flag adds to the topology problem and does not rescue the pair. No STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support exists, so nothing offsets the structural concerns. HPA's plausibility is unknown, since GPR6 has no localisation data. Brain co-expression is possible but is not enough to override an impossible interface geometry. The prediction is best treated as a spurious packing of two membrane proteins.
PTM / glycosylation
PLXNA4 has 4 glycosylation sites and GPR6 has 3 glycosylation sites plus a palmitoylation site. The fold flagged a glycosylation/lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, which AF3 does not represent. The interface itself is topologically inconsistent.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention PLXNA4 and GPR6 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR6 not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. known_interaction_strength = none.
Other subunits
NRP1
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, test the extracellular domains alone (PLXNA4 sema/PSI region with the GPR6 N-terminus and loops) and the intracellular domains alone. Then check whether a co-receptor such as a neuropilin or TREM2 changes the result. Treat the full-length prediction as unreliable.

CCL11 ↔ GPR132 CONFIRMED_NOVEL VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.56 · pTM 0.66
Rationale
CCL11 is a secreted chemokine (HPA: secreted to blood; UniProt: Secreted) and GPR132 is a 7-TM cell-membrane GPCR (UniProt), so a ligand-receptor pairing is compartment-plausible, and STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all returned nothing for the pair. Confidence is low because the fold is only marginally above threshold (ipTM 0.56, p_twoway 0.0499), CCL11's documented receptor is CCR3, GPR132 is annotated as a receptor for oxidized fatty acids and protons rather than chemokines, and both proteins carry one glycosylation site whose position relative to the modeled interface was not checked.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists the Glycoprotein keyword and 1 glycosylation site for each protein. The PubMed PTM searches were uninformative: 74 hits for CCL11 whose top titles are allergy/inflammation papers, and 1 hit for GPR132 on lactate signalling. Whether either glycan sits on the modeled interface is unknown, so this is a caveat rather than grounds for an artifact call. Neither protein's function text describes a glycan-mediated protein-binding mechanism.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for CCL11 + GPR132.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction (GPR132 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. Nothing indicates this pair is already known.
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here. (1) Inspect the AF3 model to confirm CCL11 contacts the extracellular face or TM-bundle opening of GPR132 and not cytoplasmic loops. (2) Check whether the CCL11 glycosylation site or the GPR132 glycosylation site lies in the interface, and re-fold with the glycan attached if so. (3) Counter-screen by folding CCL11 against CCR3 as a positive control and against unrelated class-A GPCRs, to see whether ipTM ~0.56 is specific or generic chemokine-GPCR docking. (4) Test experimentally with a GPR132 beta-arrestin or Gq/IP1 assay with recombinant CCL11, or a binding competition assay.

SELPLG ↔ GPR171 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.56 · pTM 0.48
Rationale
No prior evidence for the pair (STRING and CellPhoneDB miss; the single PubMed hit is a GVHD transcriptomic gene list), and both are lymphoid-enhanced membrane proteins, so the pair is novel and broadly compatible. But UniProt describes SELPLG (PSGL-1) as a SLe(x)-type proteoglycan with Glycoprotein, Sialic acid and Sulfation keywords, whose known binding is glycan- and sulfotyrosine-dependent; AF3's bare-sequence model cannot represent that. The fold is also marginal (ipTM 0.56, partner pLDDT 32.5, interface pLDDT 64.4), consistent with a large low-confidence contact (BSA 3300 Å2) on a disordered mucin-like chain.

SELPLG (UniProt): function text "SLe(x)-type proteoglycan"; keywords Glycoprotein, Sialic acid, Sulfation, Phosphoprotein; 4 annotated glycosylation sites and 6 modified residues. I'm changing the verdict. The flagged contradiction is valid: both FPR2 and GPR183 are plasma-membrane receptors and neither is secreted, so a direct contact would need both on the same cell. HPA shows no shared protein-level tissue and no overlapping enriched cell types, so the data give no route for them to meet. My earlier support was an inference from receptor class. Both are immune Gi-coupled GPCRs, and each heteromerises with other partners (FPR1 for FPR2, CXCR5 for GPR183). That does not show these two are co-expressed. Nothing else supports the pair. STRING and CellPhoneDB have no entry, and the one PubMed hit is a CD nomenclature catalogue, not an interaction report. The fold_evidence_status is not_run, so there is no structural evidence in the flagged data to offset the expression gap. The AF3 ipTM of 0.56 is modest, and 7TM bundles pack together non-specifically. I could not rule out co-expression in some monocyte or macrophage subset, so confidence is low. Rationale
The fold check shows two problems that my earlier INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict did not address. First, the modeled A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible across an intact membrane, so the contact the model proposes cannot occur in a cell. Second, a glycosylation or lipidation site lies directly on the modeled interface. AF3 does not represent glycans, so the bare-protein contact is probably not physiological. These problems fit the weak AF3 signal I had already noted (ipTM 0.56, interface pLDDT 49.4). The prior-evidence picture is unchanged: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all return nothing for this pair, and GPR21 RNA is essentially undetected in single-cell types. HPA marks the pair as plausible, but that is only weak co-presence data and does not offset a topologically impossible, low-confidence interface. I therefore treat the predicted interaction as a likely modeling artifact. I do not think "insufficient evidence" fits, because the fold evidence argues against the interaction. Confidence is medium because the check was a single fold, and a true interaction through some other interface cannot be excluded.
PTM / glycosylation
MET has 14 annotated glycosylation sites and GPR21 has 2. The fold analysis puts a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, and AF3 cannot represent glycans, so the modeled contact is unreliable.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for MET + GPR21.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found, CellPhoneDB none (GPR21 not in its table), PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. No known interaction for this pair.

TENM3 ↔ GPR21 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.56 · pTM 0.69
Rationale
The real AF3 fold shows a topology violation. The modelled TENM3–GPR21 interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, which can't happen across an intact membrane. That undermines the borderline ipTM of 0.56 and interface pLDDT of 61.6, and my earlier INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict was wrong to ignore it. The fold also places a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the interface. AF3 does not model glycans, so the contact is probably not the true binding mode, and this concern points the same way as the topology violation. Nothing independent offsets these problems: STRING and CellPhoneDB found nothing, there are 0 PubMed co-mentions, and the tissue expression profiles do not overlap (GPR21 is only weakly detected in blood vessel and TENM3 is in placenta and cerebral cortex). HPA plausibility is unknown, so I can't rely on co-localization to rescue the pair. I'm moving to IMPLAUSIBLE at medium confidence. A trans-cellular extracellular TENM3–GPR21 contact is not strictly excluded, but this model does not support one.
PTM / glycosylation
TENM3 has 17 glycosylation sites and GPR21 has 2. The fold flagged a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modelled interface. AF3 omits glycans, so the contact is unreliable.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention TENM3 and GPR21 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found, CellPhoneDB has no entry (GPR21 is not in its gene table), and PubMed co-occurrence is 0 hits. The pair is not known.
Other subunits
FLRT1;FLRT3
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, re-run AF3 with only the TENM3 extracellular domain against the GPR21 N-terminus and extracellular loops, and with glycans represented. Alternatively, test the pair experimentally with a cell-surface binding assay.

ITGA4 ↔ GPR52 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.56 · pTM 0.61
Rationale
ITGA4 is enriched in lymphoid tissue and bone marrow while GPR52 is brain-enriched at low level (5.1 nTPM) with no single-cell detection, so there is no expression overlap for two integral membrane proteins. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all return nothing, so the pair is novel but also unsupported. The fold is marginal (ipTM 0.56, interface pLDDT 63.9, min separation 1.52 Å), was run without ITGA4's obligate beta subunit, and both proteins are glycoproteins (11 and 3 annotated sites), so the large interface looks more like an artifact than a specific interaction. Confidence is low because HPA has no localisation data for GPR52 and the side of the membrane the interface sits on was not checked.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists ITGA4 as a glycoprotein with 11 glycosylation sites on its extracellular domain, and GPR52 as a glycoprotein with 3 sites. PubMed has a 2025 Nat Chem Biol paper on PTMs governing GPR52 signalling bias. A 3805 Å2 interface on ITGA4's ectodomain plausibly overlaps glycan sites that AF3 did not model; this was not checked per residue.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR52 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. Novel, but with no supporting association of any kind.
Other subunits
ITGB1;ITGB7
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here. If this is pursued, re-fold ITGA4 with ITGB1 (one representative beta subunit, not both) plus GPR52, and check whether the interface survives. Also check its membrane topology (extracellular vs cytoplasmic residues on each side) and whether annotated N-glycosylation sites fall on it. Look for GPR52 expression in ITGA4-positive cell types, or for leukocyte–neuron contact contexts, before any wet-lab work.

PPIA ↔ GPR75 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.56 · pTM 0.51
Rationale
The fold's topology check changes my view. The whole PPIA–GPR75 interface sits on the cytoplasmic face of GPR75, but the HPA data treat PPIA as a secreted protein. A secreted PPIA would meet GPR75's extracellular face, so the modeled contact can't be the way the secreted form binds. The "plausible" compartment call from HPA only reflected broad compatibility and doesn't override this. PPIA is also abundant in the cytosol, so a cytoplasmic contact isn't strictly impossible. That would be a moonlighting case, and nothing here substantiates it. STRING and CellPhoneDB have no record of the pair, PubMed co-occurrence is 0, and the confident fold is not specific to GPR75, because PPIA cleared the confidence gate against 4 of 11 receptors, which fits a sticky hub with 195 known interactions. The 3 GPR75 glycosylation sites are a minor point, because the modeled interface is cytoplasmic and glycans sit on the extracellular side. Without a specific, supported route for the two proteins to meet at this interface, I'm calling the interaction implausible, but with low confidence.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR75 has 3 glycosylation sites, but they sit on the extracellular side and the modeled interface is cytoplasmic, so this is unlikely to matter for the modeled contact.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for PPIA and GPR75.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed co-occurrence 0. No prior record of the pair (known_interaction_strength=none).
Other subunits
BSG;CCL5
Follow-up (not yet executed): If anyone wants to pursue this, test cytosolic PPIA against GPR75's intracellular loops and C-terminus (for example by co-IP or proximity labeling). Alternatively, fold the extracellular domain of GPR75 with PPIA to test the secreted-ligand scenario.

IL1RN ↔ GPR87 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.56 · pTM 0.69
Rationale
I misread the fold result in my original triage. The check shows the AF3 interface lies entirely on the cytoplasmic face of GPR87. IL1RN is a secreted protein and never reaches the cytoplasm, so the modeled contact cannot occur physically. This is a topology violation, not a pass. The ipTM of 0.56 is borderline, and the interface is unusually large. The plausible HPA rating (IL1RN secreted, GPR87 at the plasma membrane) only shows that the two could meet at the extracellular surface. The fold does not model that contact. GPR87's known ligand, LPA, binds in the transmembrane bundle, which adds no support for an IL1RN interaction. The pair has no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed trace (known_interaction_strength = none), so it is not already known. With no known interaction and a fold that models an impossible contact, the pair has no credible support as a novel interaction. A different extracellular binding mode is not excluded, but nothing in the data supports one.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists 3 glycosylation sites on GPR87 and 1 on IL1RN. None lie at the modeled interface. This is secondary to the topology problem. Neither protein is a lectin.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning both IL1RN and GPR87.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction; GPR87 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is not already known.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Validate experimentally, for example with a binding assay or a co-IP of IL1RN with GPR87-expressing cells. Re-run AF3 with several seeds to check whether the ipTM of about 0.56 and the large interface hold up. Also check whether the interface sits on the extracellular loops or reaches into the transmembrane pocket.

WNT3 ↔ GPR101 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.55 · pTM 0.59
Rationale
WNT3 (secreted) and GPR101 (orphan plasma-membrane GPCR) are a compartment-plausible ligand/receptor pair with no hit in STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed, so it is novel. However, UniProt lists WNT3 as a Lipoprotein (1 lipidation site) and Glycoprotein (2 sites), and GPR101 also has 2 glycosylation sites; AF3's bare-sequence model at a borderline ipTM of 0.55 (interface pLDDT 67.7) represents none of these. WNT3's documented receptors are Frizzleds, and GPR101 is a class A GPCR, so the modeled interface is doubtful. No fold was run, so whether any modification site actually sits on the interface is unchecked.
PTM / glycosylation
WNT3 UniProt: Lipoprotein (1 lipidation site), Glycoprotein (2 glycosylation sites), 11 disulfide bonds. PubMed includes a paper reporting that N-glycosylation of Wnt3 regulates Wnt/β-catenin signalling (PMID 38994173). GPR101 UniProt: Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites; its PubMed PTM search returned nothing relevant. Both sets of modifications are on the extracellular side where a ligand-receptor interface would form, but whether they fall on the modeled contact residues was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR101 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-fold with the WNT3 lipid and the N-glycans on both proteins represented, and check whether the interface survives and whether it sits on GPR101's extracellular face rather than spanning both sides of the membrane. Fold WNT3 against a Frizzled as a positive control and against unrelated class A GPCRs as a specificity control. If the interface persists, test experimentally with a binding assay or GPR101 signalling readout using lipidated WNT3.

NPR1 ↔ GPR146 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.55 · pTM 0.38
Rationale
I'm changing the verdict from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE, because the fold check found two structural problems that my first verdict did not address. (1) Topology violation: the modeled NPR1–GPR146 interface includes both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That cannot happen across an intact membrane, so the contact the model found is not a physically realizable binding mode. The fold was already borderline (ipTM 0.55, pTM 0.38, interface pLDDT about 60, minimum separation 1.76 Å), so the low confidence fits with the topological impossibility. (2) Glycosylation on the interface: a glycosylation or lipidation site lies directly on the modeled interface. NPR1's extracellular domain carries 7 glycosylation sites, and AF3 does not represent glycans. Any extracellular contact is therefore doubtful. This is a structural caveat, not evidence of an interaction, and it does not support LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM, because neither protein is a lectin and the topology problem already rules out the pose. Independent of the fold, nothing supports the pair. STRING and CellPhoneDB have no record of it, PubMed co-occurrence is 0, and HPA has no GPR146 subcellular data and no shared expression enrichment (plausibility unknown). I rate confidence as medium, not high, because the lack of GPR146 localization data means a real but different interaction, such as a transmembrane-helix or co-trafficking contact, cannot be excluded.
PTM / glycosylation
NPR1 has 7 glycosylation sites in its extracellular ligand-binding domain and GPR146 has 1. The fold check flagged a glycosylation/lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. AF3 omits glycans, so an extracellular contact is unreliable.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found; CellPhoneDB has no entry for the pair (GPR146 not in gene table); PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. Known-interaction strength: none, so the pair is novel but unsupported.
Other subunits
NPR1 (second protomer; functional receptor is a homodimer, per general knowledge rather than a tool result);NPPA
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, test it experimentally (co-IP or proximity ligation in cells that express both). Alternatively, re-fold only the topologically compatible domains, such as the transmembrane or extracellular regions of both proteins, with glycans modeled on the NPR1 sites.

ICAM1 ↔ GPR171 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.55 · pTM 0.58
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and both proteins are plasma-membrane proteins in the lymphoid/T-cell context, so a contact is topologically possible. However, ICAM1's ectodomain carries 8 UniProt N-glycosylation sites and GPR171 has 1, none of which AF3 modelled, and the ipTM of 0.55 is only borderline. I could not check whether any glycan site, or a mixed cytoplasmic/extracellular topology, falls on the modelled interface, so the artifact call is a caveat-driven lean rather than a demonstrated one.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists ICAM1 as a Glycoprotein with 8 glycosylation sites and 7 disulfide bonds; these sit on its Ig-domain ectodomain, the only region that could plausibly contact a GPCR's extracellular face. GPR171 is a Glycoprotein with 1 glycosylation site. The PubMed PTM search gave 1701 hits for ICAM1, but the top titles were generic inflammation papers and not informative; GPR171 gave 0. Whether any glycan site lies on the modelled interface was not checked per residue.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning ICAM1 and GPR171 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR171 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
ITGAL;ITGB2
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Map the modelled interface residues against ICAM1's N-glycosylation sites and against UniProt topology for both chains; discard the model if the interface mixes cytoplasmic and extracellular residues or is mediated by the TM helices. 2) Re-fold with core N-glycans attached on ICAM1 to see whether the interface survives. 3) Consider competition with ICAM1's established partner LFA-1 (ITGAL:ITGB2) and with GPR171's known ligand Big LEN (PCSK1N). 4) If the interface survives, test by co-IP or proximity assay in T cells.

C3 ↔ GPR174 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.55 · pTM 0.66
Rationale
The fold's topology check shows the whole modeled C3–GPR174 interface sits on GPR174's cytoplasmic face. C3 is a secreted plasma protein and cannot reach the cytoplasm, so the confident-looking pose (ipTM 0.55, interface pLDDT 68.7, min PAE 9.1) is a geometric artifact of folding a bare, full-length C3 precursor against a membrane receptor with no membrane context. I earlier overlooked this and called the pair novel on compartment grounds alone. HPA plausibility (secreted protein plus a lymphocyte surface GPCR) only shows the two could meet in principle. It cannot rescue a pose in the wrong compartment. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all found nothing, so no other evidence supports the pair. The established ligands for GPR174 are LysoPS and CCL21, and C3 fragments act through C3AR1 and C5AR2. I downgrade from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE, with medium confidence because an extracellular C3-fragment interaction was not specifically modeled.
PTM / glycosylation
Both proteins are glycosylated (C3 at 3 sites, GPR174 at 2). C3 also undergoes extensive proteolytic processing. These are secondary to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed co-mentions of C3 and GPR174.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING none, CellPhoneDB no hit (GPR174 absent from its table, so uninformative), PubMed co-occurrence 0. known_interaction_strength=none, so no known-interaction credit.
Other subunits
C3AR1;C5AR2
Follow-up (not yet executed): Optionally re-fold GPR174's extracellular face with C3a or C3a-desArg to test whether any plausible extracellular binding mode exists. Otherwise, deprioritize.

ITGAL ↔ P2RY10 LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX low confidence ipTM 0.55 · pTM 0.47
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and both are lymphoid-enhanced plasma-membrane proteins, so a cis interaction on lymphocytes is plausible. However, ITGAL is an obligate heterodimer with ITGB2 (CellPhoneDB integrin_aLb2_complex; UniProt describes all functions as ITGAL/ITGB2), and ITGB2 was absent from the model, so the contact surface may be one that ITGB2 occupies in vivo. The AF3 signal is also marginal (ipTM 0.55, interface pLDDT 59.6, min separation 1.81 Å suggesting clashes), and both proteins are glycosylated (12 and 3 annotated sites).
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: ITGAL is a Glycoprotein with 12 annotated glycosylation sites on its ectodomain; P2RY10 is a Glycoprotein with 3 sites, on its extracellular regions. The PubMed PTM search returned 7 non-specific hits for ITGAL and 0 for P2RY10. With a buried surface of 2879 Å2 and 591 contacts, any ectodomain part of the interface could plausibly overlap a glycan site; this is unverified without per-residue interface data, so it is a secondary caveat.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (P2RY10 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Other subunits
ITGB2
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here (no fold tool was available in this session). Next steps: (1) re-fold ITGAL + ITGB2 + P2RY10 and see whether the ITGAL–P2RY10 chain-pair ipTM stays at or above 0.5 and the interface avoids the ITGB2-binding surface; (2) inspect the interface topology, since a real cis interaction should be TM/TM or same-side, and any interface mixing cytoplasmic and extracellular residues is an artifact; (3) check whether ITGAL or P2RY10 N-glycosylation sites sit on the interface; (4) if it survives, test by co-IP or proximity ligation of LFA-1 and P2RY10 in primary T or B cells.

Rationale
Both are lymphoid-enriched plasma-membrane proteins (UniProt: Cell membrane) with no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed record of the pair, so the pair is biologically plausible and novel. But CD45 carries 17 annotated glycosylation sites (P2RY8 has 2) that AF3 did not model, and the fold is marginal (ipTM 0.55, interface pLDDT 60.2, min PAE 9.2 Å). The very large interface (BSA 7151 Å2, 1328 contacts) on a small 7TM receptor suggests CD45 is wrapped around the GPCR, which may involve glycan-shielded ectodomain or a topologically impossible contact; I did not run a fold to check which side the interface is on.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: PTPRC is a Glycoprotein with 17 glycosylation sites (heavily N- and O-glycosylated ectodomain; its CLEC10A interaction is glycan-mediated via Tn antigen) plus 9 modified residues. P2RY8 is a Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites on its extracellular portion. The PubMed PTM searches returned mostly unrelated hits. Any ectodomain contact in the bare-sequence model is plausibly glycan-shielded in vivo; this is not confirmed per residue.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (P2RY8 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel as far as these sources show.

Rationale
The fold check I originally lacked has now been run, and it flags two problems. First, the modeled A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible for two single intact membrane proteins, because no one contact surface can sit on both sides of the bilayer. Second, a glycosylation or lipidation site lies directly on the modeled interface, and AF3 does not represent glycans, so the contact may be blocked in reality. Together with the marginal confidence (ipTM 0.55, partner pLDDT 51.3), these show the predicted pose is an artifact rather than a real membrane-plane interface. The other evidence is weak support at best: both proteins are lymphoid plasma-membrane receptors (HPA plausibility = plausible), but there is no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed trace for the pair. Co-expression alone does not rescue a topologically invalid pose. I am therefore moving from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE for this modeled interaction. The verdict is medium confidence because a genuine cis association through a different, topology-consistent interface is not formally excluded.
PTM / glycosylation
TNFRSF1B has 6 glycosylation sites and P2RY8 has 2. The fold analysis places a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, so the bare-sequence AF3 contact is likely unreliable.
PubMed co-occurrence

STRING / CellPhoneDB

C5AR1 ↔ GPR141 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.54 · pTM 0.63
Rationale
The fold check found a topology violation: the modeled A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That cannot happen across an intact membrane, because two GPCRs in one bilayer can only meet laterally, through TM-TM contacts or contacts on the same side. My original call did not account for this, so the "CONFIRMED_NOVEL" verdict is withdrawn. The ipTM of 0.54 was already marginal and the interface pLDDT was about 71, so nothing offsets this concern. This is a weak, geometrically impossible pose, not support for a specific heterodimer. The known-interaction evidence stays at none: STRING and CellPhoneDB had no hit and PubMed had 0 co-mentions, so novelty credit is not at issue here. The original co-expression argument (both in myeloid/bone marrow) is only generic plausibility. HPA plausibility is unknown, since GPR141 has no localization data, so it cannot rescue the fold. The glycosylation caveat is unchanged and minor. A real C5AR1–GPR141 heterodimer is not ruled out, but this AF3 model does not support one.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: C5AR1 is a glycoprotein (1 glycosylation site) with sulfation and 11 modified residues; GPR141 is a glycoprotein (2 glycosylation sites). The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to an interface (C5AR1 40 generic hits, GPR141 1 unrelated hit). These modifications probably sit on the extracellular N-terminus/loops or cytoplasmic tail rather than a lateral TM-TM interface, but site positions were not checked against the modeled contacts, so this is an unresolved minor caveat, not grounds for an artifact call.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning C5AR1 and GPR141 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found; CellPhoneDB none (GPR141 absent); PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. Known interaction strength: none.

GLG1 ↔ GPR75 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.54 · pTM 0.59
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and compartments are compatible, but both are glycoproteins (UniProt: GLG1 5 glycosylation sites plus sialic acid; GPR75 3 sites) and AF3 folded bare sequence at only borderline confidence (ipTM 0.54, interface pLDDT 62.6, min separation 1.89 Å). I could not run a fold to check whether any glycan site sits on the interface or which membrane side it falls on, so the artifact call is an inference, not a per-residue finding.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: GLG1 carries the Glycoprotein and Sialic acid keywords with 5 annotated glycosylation sites; GPR75 carries Glycoprotein with 3 sites. PubMed supports GLG1 glycan modification (FUT3-synthesised Lewis-a on GLG1; polysialylation and shedding of E-selectin ligand-1); the GPR75 PubMed hits were 20-HETE signalling papers, not PTM-specific. GLG1's stated function is binding E-selectin, a lectin, so its recognised binding mode is glycan-dependent. By inference, a 5550 Å2 interface with 1104 contacts must involve GLG1's large luminal domain, since its cytoplasmic tail is very short, and so would face GPR75's glycosylated extracellular side. Whether a glycan site actually lies on the modeled interface was not verified.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for GLG1 + GPR75.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported. UniProt gives GPR75's activator as CCL5/RANTES, and GLG1's partners as fibroblast growth factor and E-selectin.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Map the AF3 interface residues against UniProt N-glycosylation sites and topology for Q92896 (GLG1) and O95800 (GPR75), and confirm the interface does not mix cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. 2) If a glycan site is on the interface, re-fold with the core N-glycans attached and see whether the interface survives. 3) Inspect the model for clashes (min separation 1.89 Å) and for a diffuse wrap-around interface, which the very large buried area with only moderate pLDDT suggests. 4) If the interface holds up, test by co-immunoprecipitation or proximity labelling in neuronal or retinal cells expressing GPR75.

RNASET2 ↔ GPR82 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.54 · pTM 0.7
Rationale
The fold check shows the RNASET2–GPR82 interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues of GPR82. That is topologically impossible for a secreted protein, since RNASET2 cannot reach the cytoplasmic face of an intact membrane. My original CONFIRMED_NOVEL verdict relied on compartment plausibility (secreted ligand, membrane GPCR) and a borderline ipTM of 0.54, and it did not account for this. The compartment argument still holds in principle, but the modeled pose does not support it, and ipTM 0.54 gives no independent reason to trust the pose. The novelty finding is unchanged: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned nothing, so this is not a known interaction. Novelty alone is not evidence of a real interaction. The glycosylation caveat is also unresolved: neither protein is a lectin, but AF3 omits glycans. With the geometry violated and no supporting expression data, I downgrade to IMPLAUSIBLE (medium confidence), because only the modeled pose has been ruled out and a true extracellular-only contact is not excluded.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: RNASET2 is a glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites and 4 disulfide bonds; GPR82 is a glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. PubMed PTM search: 8 hits for RNASET2 (mostly not about its own glycosylation; one on expression in CHO-S cells), 0 for GPR82. Neither protein's function text describes a glycan-mediated binding mechanism (RNASET2 is an RNA-cleaving enzyme). Whether any glycosylation site lies on the modeled interface is unknown; this is an unresolved caveat, not evidence of an artifact.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count = 0 for RNASET2 and GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found (GPR82 is not in the gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. Known-interaction strength is none, so no ALREADY_KNOWN credit applies.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-fold RNASET2 against only the GPR82 extracellular regions (N-terminus and extracellular loops) and check whether a topologically valid contact still scores well. Include glycosylation if possible.

ITGAM is an obligate heterodimer with ITGB2 (CellPhoneDB integrin_aMb2_complex), and ITGB2 was absent from the model, so the borderline fold (ipTM 0.54, interface pLDDT 61.7, min separation 1.79 Å) may be using surface that ITGB2 normally occupies. The pair is unreported (STRING none, CellPhoneDB none, PubMed 0), but it is not supported well enough to call novel: ITGAM carries 19 glycosylation sites, and the two proteins are enriched in different immune cell types.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: ITGAM is a glycoprotein with 19 annotated glycosylation sites and 10 disulfides on its ectodomain; P2RY10 is a glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM search gave 24 hits for ITGAM (the titles shown are not glycosylation-specific) and 0 for P2RY10. Heavy N-glycosylation of the ITGAM ectodomain could plausibly occlude a large modeled extracellular interface; whether any site lies on the interface was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for ITGAM + P2RY10.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction (P2RY10 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
ITGB2
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run for this triage. Re-fold ITGAM + ITGB2 + P2RY10 and see whether the ITGAM–P2RY10 chain-pair ipTM stays at or above 0.5 with ITGB2 present. In that model, check the interface topology (it must not mix cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, or bury TM helices implausibly) and whether any of ITGAM's 19 or P2RY10's 3 N-glycosylation sites sit on the interface. The 1.79 Å minimum separation suggests clashes, so inspect the structure directly. A CORUM/STRING complex check would also help.

PTPRC ↔ GPR171 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.53 · pTM 0.53
Rationale
Both are plasma-membrane proteins of lymphoid cells (GPR171 is T/NK-cell enhanced; PTPRC/CD45 is pan-leukocyte), so a cis interaction on T cells is physically possible, and STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed (0 hits) show no prior report. However, CD45 carries 17 annotated glycosylation sites on its ectodomain, which AF3 did not model, and the fold is only borderline (ipTM 0.53, interface pLDDT 67.7, minimum interface PAE 9.83 Å) with a very large, diffuse interface (BSA 5835 Å2, 1054 contacts). I could not check which side of the membrane the interface sits on, so the glycan-artifact call is an inference, not a verified finding.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt PTPRC: Glycoprotein keyword, 17 glycosylation sites and 9 modified residues; its function text describes CLEC10A recognising Tn-antigen glycans on CD45, i.e. glycan-mediated ectodomain interactions. UniProt GPR171: Glycoprotein, 1 glycosylation site. The PubMed PTM search for PTPRC returned 33 hits, but the titles shown are unrelated to glycosylation; GPR171 returned 0. A 5835 Å2 interface that includes the CD45 ectodomain would very likely overlap glycan-occupied surface, but the per-residue interface location was not verified.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning PTPRC and GPR171 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR171 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel as far as these sources go.
Other subunits
CD22;BCR
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold tool was available in this session, so the interface side and glycan overlap remain untested. Next steps: (1) map the AF3 interface residues onto CD45 topology (ectodomain vs TM vs cytoplasmic phosphatase domains) and onto GPR171's faces, and reject the model if it touches both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues; (2) if the interface is on the ectodomain, re-fold with N-glycans at the CD45 sites and see whether it survives; (3) if it is cytoplasmic (phosphatase domains on the GPCR intracellular face), re-fold with only the CD45 cytoplasmic region plus GPR171 to see whether ipTM improves; (4) test by co-IP or proximity labelling in primary T cells. The CellPhoneDB complex BCR_CD45_CD22 is B-cell specific and is listed in other_subunits only for completeness; it is not a relevant missing subunit for a T-cell GPCR.

CEACAM8 ↔ GPR33 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.53 · pTM 0.63
Rationale
The fold check shows two problems that my first INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict did not address. First, the modeled A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is impossible across an intact membrane, so the borderline AF3 contact (ipTM 0.53, interface pLDDT 61.7) is not a physically realizable binding mode. Second, a glycosylation or lipidation site sits directly on the modeled interface. AF3 does not represent glycans or the GPI anchor, so the contact is more likely a bare-sequence artifact than a real interface. Nothing else supports the pair: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no record (known_interaction_strength=none), and GPR33 RNA is not detected in any HPA tissue or cell type (hpa_plausibility=unknown). With no co-expression, no literature and a topologically invalid low-confidence fold, I now rate the interaction implausible rather than merely under-evidenced. Medium confidence, because GPR33 expression data is sparse and a different topology-compatible interaction (extracellular only) cannot be fully excluded.
PTM / glycosylation
CEACAM8 has 11 glycosylation sites plus a GPI anchor, and GPR33 has 4 glycosylation sites. The fold analysis found a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. AF3 does not model these modifications, so the contact is unreliable.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: no interaction. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported, so known_interaction_strength=none.
Other subunits
CEACAM6;CEACAM1
Follow-up (not yet executed): If the pair is still of interest, re-run AF3 using only the extracellular domains (CEACAM8 ectodomain with the GPR33 N-terminus) and check whether a topology-consistent interface persists. LGALS3 ↔ GPR39 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM medium confidence ipTM 0.53 · pTM 0.61
Rationale
Compartments are compatible (secreted galectin-3, plasma-membrane GPCR GPR39) and the pair is unreported (no STRING or CellPhoneDB hit; one incidental PubMed co-mention). But UniProt describes LGALS3 as a "galactose-specific lectin" and GPR39 as a glycoprotein with 3 annotated glycosylation sites, so any real binding would most likely be glycan-mediated, which AF3's bare-sequence fold cannot represent. The fold itself is also borderline (ipTM 0.53, interface pLDDT 66.8).
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: LGALS3 function is "Galactose-specific lectin" (keyword Lectin), so its binding to surface receptors is canonically glycan-mediated. GPR39 carries the Glycoprotein keyword and 3 annotated glycosylation sites; their position (presumably the extracellular N-terminus or loops) was not confirmed. The pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits for both genes (39 and 25) were non-specific and added nothing. The mechanism-level concern stands regardless of which residues AF3 placed in contact.
PubMed co-occurrence
One PubMed hit (PMID 40616194, an omics gene list in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia). This is an unrelated co-mention, not evidence of a direct interaction.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction. PubMed: one co-mention, a methylation/transcriptomics study of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, not a binding report. The pair is effectively novel in the literature.
Other subunits
HTR1A;GALR1
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run in this triage. Next steps: (1) re-fold with the N-glycans attached at GPR39's 3 UniProt sites and check whether the LGALS3 carbohydrate-recognition domain engages the glycan rather than the modeled protein surface; (2) check the interface topology to confirm the contact is on GPR39's extracellular side and not on both sides of the membrane; (3) test in the wet lab with lactose-competition or PNGase-treated binding assays to separate glycan-dependent from protein-protein binding. The other_subunits listed are the heteroreceptor partners named in UniProt's GPR39 function text, not CellPhoneDB complex members (no complex was found there).

SLIT2 ↔ GPR52 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.53 · pTM 0.39
Rationale
My original rationale said the fold showed no topology violation. The check shows the opposite: the real AF3 fold put the whole SLIT2–GPR52 interface on GPR52's cytoplasmic face. SLIT2 is secreted and never reaches the cytoplasm, so the modeled contact is topologically impossible. The weak scores (ipTM 0.53, pTM 0.39, interface pLDDT 67) fit a spurious placement. The other evidence doesn't rescue it. There is no STRING or CellPhoneDB hit and 0 PubMed co-mentions, so nothing known supports the pair. The 'plausible' HPA co-expression only shows the two are present in the same tissues. It doesn't make a cytoplasmic-face contact possible. An extracellular SLIT2–GPR52 contact would need a different interface from the one modeled. Nothing in the data supports one. Neither protein is a lectin, so a glycan-mediated mode isn't relevant here.
PTM / glycosylation
No annotated PTM or glycosylation site lies on the modeled interface. Neither protein is a lectin. This is not the main issue. The topology violation is.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for SLIT2 and GPR52.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING none, CellPhoneDB none (GPR52 not in its gene table), PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. There is no prior support for this pair.
Other subunits
ROBO1
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, re-fold SLIT2 with only the GPR52 extracellular N-terminus and loops, or mask the cytoplasmic face. Treat the pair as supported only if a confident extracellular interface appears.

Rationale
The AF3 fold has now run. It flagged a glycosylation or lipidation site sitting directly on the modeled PPIA–GPR82 interface. My earlier note said interface overlap had not been checked, so this closes that gap, and it counts against the pose. AF3 models bare sequence only. A modified residue at the contact means the predicted pose may be an artifact of leaving the glycan out. It may also be a contact that the real glycan would block or change. The concern also fits what I already knew: GPR82 has 2 glycosylation sites on its extracellular face, and PPIA binds heparan sulfate. PPIA reached the confidence gate against 4 of 11 receptors, and ipTM was borderline at 0.53. That points to a promiscuous, sticky hub protein rather than a specific interaction. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no prior report (known_interaction_strength=none), so the pair is not already known. HPA says the two proteins could plausibly meet (secreted PPIA, membrane GPR82), but that does not show specificity. Together this supports LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM over INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
PTM / glycosylation
The fold-level check found a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. GPR82 is a glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites, and PPIA binds heparan sulfate. AF3 cannot represent these modifications, so the interface contact is unreliable as modeled.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for PPIA + GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING shows no association, CellPhoneDB has no curated interaction, and PubMed co-occurrence is 0 papers. The pair is not previously reported.
Other subunits
BSG
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-run the fold with the glycan or lipid modification represented on the flagged GPR82 residue. Alternatively, mask the site and see whether the PPIA contact persists. Check whether PPIA reaches the confidence gate against unrelated GPCRs as a control.
