CCL28 ↔ GPRC5A IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.53 · pTM 0.65
Rationale
The AF3 fold's topology check shows the CCL28–GPRC5A interface lies entirely on the cytoplasmic face of GPRC5A. CCL28 is a secreted chemokine and is never in the cytoplasm, so the predicted contact cannot happen physiologically. This undercuts the original CONFIRMED_NOVEL call. The compartment-level argument (secreted ligand, surface receptor) held only if the contact was extracellular, and the fold puts it on the wrong side of the membrane. The ipTM of 0.53 is marginal and doesn't offset this. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all show no known interaction, so the pair is novel in the literature, but that gives no support for a real contact. I rate this IMPLAUSIBLE rather than novel. I'm only at medium confidence because an extracellular binding mode was not tested and the fold used a bare sequence.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists both as Glycoprotein with one glycosylation site each; GPRC5A also has 6 modified residues (Phosphoprotein keyword). The PubMed PTM searches returned only non-specific hits (biomarker and cancer papers), nothing on glycosylation of either protein. The GPRC5A glycosylation site may lie in its extracellular region and could sit near a chemokine-binding surface, but its position relative to the modeled interface was not checked (no fold or per-residue tool was available). A single glycan on each side is a caveat, not enough for an artifact call.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for CCL28 and GPRC5A.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING not found, CellPhoneDB none (GPRC5A is not in its gene table), PubMed co-occurrence 0 hits. There is no prior evidence for this pair.
Follow-up (not yet executed): If this pair is still of interest, re-fold CCL28 against only the extracellular N-terminal domain and loops of GPRC5A. Alternatively, test the known receptors CCR3 and CCR10 as a control. Do not rely on the current cytoplasmic-face pose.

ICOSLG ↔ GPR34 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.59
Rationale
No prior evidence for this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB no match, PubMed 0 hits), and compartments/expression are compatible, so it is novel and not implausible. But ipTM is borderline (0.52), and UniProt lists both as glycoproteins with 5 glycosylation sites each, which the bare-sequence AF3 model does not represent. GPR34 is a lysophosphatidylserine (lipid) GPCR with no known protein ligand, and the large interface (BSA 2816 Å2, 648 contacts) may be transmembrane-helix packing made without a bilayer; I could not check where the interface falls because no fold was run.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: ICOSLG has the Glycoprotein keyword and 5 glycosylation sites (on its Ig ectodomain, by my reading of the topology); GPR34 has the Glycoprotein keyword and 5 glycosylation sites (on its extracellular N-terminus/loops, likewise inferred). The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing relevant (ICOSLG 1 unrelated hit; GPR34 8 hits on pharmacology and lymphoma). Any extracellular interface would likely involve glycosylated regions on both sides, but whether a site sits on the modeled interface was not verified.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction match (GPR34 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel as far as these sources go.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Inspect the AF3 model to see whether the interface is transmembrane-helix packing or ectodomain contact, and whether it mixes cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. Map the UniProt N-glycosylation sites of both proteins onto the interface, and if any land on it, re-fold with glycans attached. Canonical ICOSLG–ICOS binding and LysoPS–GPR34 binding are the expected real interactions; a wet-lab test (co-immunoprecipitation or a cell-surface binding assay in macrophages) is needed before pursuing this pair.

MST1 ↔ GPR37 CONFIRMED_NOVEL VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.55
Rationale
HPA classes MST1 (macrophage stimulating 1) as secreted to blood and GPR37 as a membrane GPCR, so a ligand-receptor pairing is topologically plausible, and STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned no hit for the pair. Confidence is low because the AF3 ipTM of 0.52 is only just above the 0.5 threshold, the supplied p_twoway is 0.050, and the glycosylation caveat on GPR37 could not be checked against the interface. The MST1 UniProt lookup returned the wrong protein (STK4, the Hippo kinase aliased "MST1", Q13043), so no valid UniProt mechanism or PTM data was obtained for the MST1 side.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR37: UniProt lists the Glycoprotein keyword and 3 glycosylation sites, and the extracellular side is where a secreted ligand would bind, so a glycan at the modelled interface is possible but was not verified. MST1: uniprot_annotation returned STK4 (Q13043), not the macrophage stimulating protein, so its PTM data does not apply; the pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits for MST1 (406) are likewise dominated by STK4/Hippo papers and are uninformative. No per-residue interface check was done, so there is not enough to call LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits. The symbol "MST1" is ambiguous with STK4 in the literature, so even a nonzero count would have needed disambiguation.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No evidence anywhere of a known interaction. UniProt lists prosaposin, osteocalcin and neuroprotectin D1 as GPR37 ligands; MST1 is not among them.
Other subunits
MST1R
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Re-pull UniProt for the correct MST1 protein (macrophage stimulating protein, P26927 from background knowledge) to get its glycosylation sites and domain structure. 2) MST1R (RON) is listed under other_subunits from background knowledge as the established MST1 receptor, not from any tool result; fold MST1–MST1R as a positive-control benchmark for the 0.52 ipTM. 3) Check whether the modelled interface falls on GPR37's extracellular N-terminus or loops rather than cytoplasmic residues, and whether any of the 3 GPR37 N-glycosylation sites sit on it; if so, re-fold with the glycan attached. 4) Test binding and signalling experimentally, e.g. MST1-induced ERK phosphorylation or internalisation in GPR37-expressing cells, with prosaposin as a positive control.

In addition, the increased macrophage phagocytosis mediates protection against sepsis upon pathogen infection. CHRNE ↔ GPRC5A IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.61
Rationale
No database or literature support (STRING and CellPhoneDB misses, 0 PubMed co-mentions) and no overlap in HPA tissue enrichment (CHRNE heart muscle/pituitary; GPRC5A lung/urinary bladder). CHRNE is an obligate subunit of the muscle nAChR pentamer (CHRNA1/CHRNB1/CHRND per CellPhoneDB), so folding it alone exposes inter-subunit surfaces that are buried in vivo; a borderline ipTM of 0.52 between two multi-pass membrane proteins most likely reflects non-specific helix packing. The pair is novel, but the evidence does not support it as a real interaction.
PTM / glycosylation
Both are UniProt glycoproteins (CHRNE 2 glycosylation sites, GPRC5A 1 site plus 6 modified residues). The PubMed PTM searches returned only unrelated disease and cancer papers. Whether any glycosylation site lies on the modeled interface was not checked; this is a secondary concern behind the missing subunits and lack of coexpression.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed co-mentions.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction; GPRC5A is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
CHRNA1;CHRNB1;CHRND
Follow-up (not yet executed): If pursued, check where the modeled GPRC5A contact sits on CHRNE: if it falls on surfaces that CHRNA1/CHRND occupy in the assembled (α1)2β1δε pentamer, it is an artifact of folding an isolated subunit. Also check interface topology for mixed cytoplasmic/extracellular contacts, and whether GPRC5A is expressed in skeletal muscle or at the neuromuscular junction at all. No fold was run for this candidate.

Rationale
The check says HPA gives no route for these two to meet. Neither protein is secreted, so contact would need them in the same place, and HPA shows zero shared protein-level tissue (PLXNB3 in brain/glia, GPRC5A in lung/bladder). Both are plasma-membrane proteins, so there is no compartment mismatch. That only makes a meeting possible in principle, and nothing observed supports it. The data also give no positive evidence: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned nothing for this pair (known_interaction_strength=none), and the AF3 model was marginal (ipTM 0.52, interface pLDDT 60.2, minimum interface PAE 10.46 Å). The flagged fold status is "not_run", so there is no separate structural result to weigh. PLXNB3's 8 glycosylation sites are unrepresented in AF3, which weakens the model further. I am moving from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE because the absence of shared tissue combined with the weak model leaves no substantiated reason to expect these proteins to interact. Confidence stays low because HPA tissue data are coarse and low-level co-expression in some cells cannot be ruled out.
PTM / glycosylation
PLXNB3 has 8 glycosylation sites that AF3 does not represent. GPRC5A has 1 glycosylation site. Whether any lie on the interface was not checked per residue.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-mention count is 0 for PLXNB3 and GPRC5A.
STRING / CellPhoneDB

TLR8 ↔ P2RY8 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.66
Rationale
UniProt places TLR8 in the endosome (an ssRNA sensor that homodimerises) and P2RY8 at the cell membrane (a GPCR for the metabolite GGG), so the two do not share a compartment by annotation. TLR8's ectodomain carries 21 annotated N-glycosylation sites that AF3 did not model, and the ipTM of 0.52 is only just at threshold. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed (0 hits) give no supporting evidence; this is novel but not well supported rather than strictly ruled out, since HPA has no localisation data for either protein.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt annotates TLR8 as a glycoprotein with 21 glycosylation sites and 6 disulfide bonds; these sit on the luminal LRR ectodomain, which makes up most of the protein and is the likely modelled contact surface. P2RY8 is a glycoprotein with 2 sites. The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to this interface. Whether any glycan site lies on the modelled interface was not checked, because no fold was run.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no hit (P2RY8 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is novel, with no literature support.

CHL1 ↔ GPR6 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.49
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and compartment-plausible: both are brain-expressed, CHL1 is a secreted/membrane adhesion protein and GPR6 a plasma-membrane GPCR. However, UniProt lists both as glycoproteins (CHL1 10 glycosylation sites, GPR6 3 plus a palmitoylation site), which AF3's bare-sequence model omits, and the fold is only marginal (ipTM 0.51, interface pLDDT 64.7). Whether any glycan actually sits on the modeled interface was not checked, so the artifact call is a caveat rather than a demonstrated result.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: CHL1 carries the Glycoprotein keyword with 10 annotated glycosylation sites and 6 disulfide bonds; GPR6 is a Glycoprotein (3 sites) and a palmitoylated Lipoprotein (1 lipidation site). The pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits were mostly off-target (plant CHL1/NRT1.1 papers; general GPR6 expression papers) and add little. The large modeled interface (BSA 2276 Å2, 307 contacts) on glycosylated proteins makes glycan interference plausible, but no per-residue check of glycan sites against the interface was done.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning CHL1 and GPR6 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction, and GPR6 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Map the AF3 interface residues against the UniProt N-glycosylation sites of CHL1 (O00533) and GPR6 (P46095), and against GPR6 membrane topology, to confirm the contact is purely extracellular and not glycan-occluded. If a glycan sits on the interface, re-fold with it attached. Given the marginal ipTM (0.51), an orthogonal binding assay is needed before pursuing this pair, for example soluble CHL1 ectodomain on GPR6-expressing cells with a cAMP readout, since GPR6 is constitutively active and its proposed agonists are lipids.

TNC ↔ GPR75 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.39
Rationale
The pair is compartment-plausible (TNC secreted to the extracellular matrix, GPR75 a plasma-membrane GPCR) and has no hit in STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed, so it is novel. However, TNC is a heavily glycosylated proteoglycan (24 UniProt glycosylation sites) and GPR75 carries 3 glycosylation sites, none of which AF3 modeled. The supplied fold metrics are also weak: ipTM 0.51 is borderline, interface pLDDT is 57.7, min separation of 1.55 Å indicates clashes, and a 7229 Å2 interface with 1587 contacts is implausibly large for a GPCR's small ectodomain, so it probably spans transmembrane or cytoplasmic regions a secreted protein cannot reach.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt annotates TNC as Glycoprotein and Proteoglycan with 24 glycosylation sites and 42 disulfide bonds, and GPR75 as Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites. Both sets of glycans are on the extracellular surfaces where any real contact would occur, so they are plausibly relevant to the modeled interface. The PubMed PTM searches (134 hits for TNC, 11 for GPR75) returned nothing specific to glycosylation. No per-residue check of glycan sites against the interface was done.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers co-mention TNC and GPR75.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel. UniProt lists integrins (alpha-8/beta-1, alpha-9/beta-1, alpha-V/beta-3, alpha-V/beta-6) as TNC's receptors and CCL5 as GPR75's activating ligand.
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here. Re-fold a truncated construct (individual TNC domains such as the FN-III repeats or fibrinogen globe against GPR75) rather than the 2741-token full complex. Then check the interface topology (extracellular only versus transmembrane/cytoplasmic) and whether the N-glycan sites on GPR75's N-terminus and extracellular loops, or on TNC, fall on the interface. If a confident extracellular interface survives (chain-pair ipTM above 0.5, no clashes), re-fold with glycans attached before any wet-lab binding assay.

B2M ↔ GPR82 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.67
Rationale
The fold check shows a glycosylation/lipidation site lying directly on the modeled B2M–GPR82 interface. My earlier CONFIRMED_NOVEL verdict left this unchecked, and the flagged site undercuts it. AF3 models bare sequence, so a contact that runs through a glycosylated residue (GPR82 has 2 UniProt glycosylation sites, likely on the extracellular face) may not be a real binding mode. The glycan could block the contact or change it. The pair is still novel, with no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed trace (known_interaction_strength=none). HPA compartment plausibility holds, since B2M is secreted and GPR82 is on the membrane. But ipTM 0.51, interface pLDDT 64.9 and min PAE 9.3 Å are weak, so the interface is not strong enough to outweigh the PTM concern. I therefore downgrade to a PTM-caveated artifact. The confident-novel call is not justified.
PTM / glycosylation
The AF3 fold analysis flagged a glycosylation/lipidation site directly on the modeled interface. GPR82 has 2 UniProt glycosylation sites, plausibly on its extracellular face. B2M has 7 "Glycosylation" features, which I read as glycation (my own interpretation). Because AF3 omits glycans, the modeled contact may not reflect the real binding mode.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for B2M with GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction, and GPR82 is absent from its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0. So the pair is novel as far as known-interaction evidence goes.
Other subunits
FCGRT;CD1B
Follow-up (not yet executed): Locate the GPR82 glycosylation site positions relative to the interface. Re-fold with the glycan represented, or with the site mutated. Test B2M together with an MHC-I heavy chain, since B2M normally exists in that complex.

IGF2R ↔ GPR82 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.66
Rationale
No prior evidence links this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, 0 PubMed co-mentions), and expression/compartment do not rule it out. However, IGF2R's documented binding mechanism is lectin-type (mannose-6-phosphate recognition) and its ectodomain carries 18 annotated glycosylation sites, while GPR82 has 2 on its small extracellular surface; AF3's bare-sequence model represents none of this. The fold itself is also weak (ipTM 0.51 at the threshold, interface pLDDT 52.4, min separation 1.79 Å suggesting clashes), so the modeled interface is not trustworthy as drawn. I could not check whether any glycosylation site actually sits on the modeled interface, so the artifact call rests on general plausibility, not a per-residue finding.
PTM / glycosylation
IGF2R (UniProt P11717): Glycoprotein, Lipoprotein/Palmitate; 18 glycosylation sites, 59 disulfide bonds; function is binding phosphomannosyl (M6P) residues on lysosomal enzymes, i.e. a glycan-mediated mechanism. GPR82 (Q96P67): Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM search gave 56 hits for IGF2R (the top titles are mostly not about PTMs) and 0 for GPR82. With about 2,832 Å² of buried surface on the heavily glycosylated IGF2R ectodomain, glycan interference at the modeled contact is plausible, but whether any site lies on the interface was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning IGF2R and GPR82 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction found (GPR82 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported; GPR82 is an orphan receptor per UniProt.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Map the modeled interface residues against IGF2R's 18 and GPR82's 2 UniProt N-glycosylation sites, and check membrane topology of the interface (that it does not combine cytoplasmic and extracellular residues). Re-fold using only the relevant IGF2R domain repeats plus GPR82, with glycans attached, to see whether ipTM rises clearly above 0.5; the current 2,827-token fold with interface pLDDT 52 and 1.79 Å minimum separation is marginal. IGF2R has 116 known interactors (HPA), so a promiscuous or non-specific contact with a large ectodomain is also possible. If the interface survives, test by co-immunoprecipitation in macrophage/Kupffer-like cells.

CSPG4 ↔ MRGPRF IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.44
Rationale
I'm changing the verdict from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE, because two points now count against the pair and nothing counts for it. (1) Neither protein is secreted, and HPA shows no shared protein-level tissue. The only overlap is RNA-level, in smooth muscle cells and pericytes. I had treated that overlap and the poor antibody coverage for GPCRs as reasons to stay neutral. Without protein evidence, though, there is no substantiated way for the two to meet. Being plasma-membrane proteins in general does not supply one. (2) A real AF3 fold was run, which my original triage did not account for. It placed the A–B interface across both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is topologically impossible across an intact membrane, so the predicted contact is not a physical interaction. The interface also sits on a glycosylation or lipidation site, and AF3 does not model those modifications. The pair has no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support, and no other evidence offsets these concerns. Confidence is medium and not high because the HPA gap partly reflects limited antibody coverage and RNA overlap does exist.
PTM / glycosylation
CSPG4 has 16 glycosylation sites and MRGPRF has 1. The fold flagged a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface, so the bare-sequence contact is unreliable. Neither protein is a lectin.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for CSPG4 + MRGPRF.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence returned nothing for this pair, so it is novel with no literature support. MRGPRF is an orphan receptor.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Check for protein-level co-localization of CSPG4 and MRGPRF in pericytes or vascular smooth muscle cells. Only if that is shown, re-fold with the ectodomains alone, so the interface cannot span the membrane, and model the glycans.

Collaborates with CXCR5 to mediate B-cell migration; probably by forming a heterodimer with CXCR5 that affects the interaction between of CXCL13 and CXCR5 (PubMed:22913878). Also acts as a chemotactic receptor for some T-cells upon binding to 7-alpha,25-OHC ligand (By similarity). Expression in splenic dendritic cells is required for their homeostasis, localization and ability to induce B- and T-cell responses: GPR183 acts as a chemotactic receptor in dendritic cells that mediates the accumulation of CD4(+) dendritic cells in bridging channels (By similarity). Regulates migration of astrocytes and is involved in communication between astrocytes and macrophages (PubMed:25297897). Promotes osteoclast precursor migration to bone surfaces (By similarity). TFR2 ↔ GPR22 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.5 · pTM 0.67
Rationale
Both are integral membrane proteins (TFR2 single-pass type II, GPR22 a 7TM orphan GPCR), so a cis interaction needs the same cell, but HPA shows no overlap: TFR2 is liver-enriched (hepatocytes, erythrocyte progenitors) and GPR22 is in brain neurons and cardiomyocytes. The AF3 signal is borderline (ipTM 0.5, interface pLDDT 59.3, min separation 1.82 Å with 615 contacts and 3204 Å2 buried), which looks more like non-specific membrane-protein packing than a real interface. No STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support exists; confidence is low because HPA has no localisation data for GPR22 and no fold was run to check interface topology.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists both as glycoproteins: TFR2 has 4 glycosylation sites on its ectodomain and GPR22 has 2. The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to glycosylation of either protein at an interface. Glycans on the extracellular regions are an extra caveat for any modeled ectodomain contact, but the verdict does not rest on this.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-mention count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction, and GPR22 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported, but that novelty is not backed by biological plausibility.
Other subunits
TFRC;HFE;TF
Follow-up (not yet executed): Deprioritise. The other_subunits listed are TFR2's physiological partners from general knowledge (it is a homodimer that binds transferrin and HFE), not from a tool result; CellPhoneDB returned no complex for either protein. If the pair is revisited, inspect the model for which regions form the interface (TM helix against TM helix, or an interface mixing cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, would indicate an artifact) and check whether the TFR2 glycosylation sites sit on it. Any real co-expression would most plausibly be in cardiomyocytes or neurons, where TFR2 is low, and should be confirmed before any wet-lab work.

CTSG ↔ GPR34 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.5 · pTM 0.54
Rationale
My original rationale said the fold showed no topology violation. The check shows that was wrong. The fold put the CTSG–GPR34 interface on GPR34's cytoplasmic face. CTSG is a secreted granule protease with no membrane topology and no evidence of cytosolic localisation, so it cannot reach that face. The modeled contact is therefore not physically achievable, and the borderline confidence (ipTM about 0.5, interface pLDDT about 63) cannot rescue it. The remaining evidence is too thin to override this. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed show nothing for the pair (known_interaction_strength=none), and HPA co-expression is unknown, so nothing places the two proteins together. The only support is indirect: CTSG cleaves other GPCRs such as PAR1 and PAR4. A real interaction with GPR34's extracellular face stays conceivable, but this fold doesn't model it. I rate the modeled interaction implausible, with low confidence because that extracellular-face possibility was not tested.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR34 has 5 UniProt N-glycosylation sites and CTSG has 2. None lie at the modeled interface. Neither protein is a lectin. The PTM concern is not the problem here; the topology violation is.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention CTSG and GPR34 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence returned nothing for this pair (known_interaction_strength=none). CTSG acting on PAR1, PAR4 and FPR1 is only indirect precedent.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-fold with constraints or a truncated GPR34 extracellular region (N-terminus and loops) against CTSG. Check whether a docked pose on the extracellular face is confident. Look at HPA immune-cell co-expression, for example neutrophils and mast cells.

Prefers Phe and Tyr residues in the P1 position of substrates but also cleaves efficiently after Trp and Leu (PubMed:29652924). Shows a preference for negatively charged amino acids in the P2' position and for aliphatic amino acids both upstream and downstream of the cleavage site (PubMed:29652924). Required for recruitment and activation of platelets which is mediated by the F2RL3/PAR4 platelet receptor (PubMed:10702240, PubMed:3390156). Binds reversibly to and stimulates B cells and CD4(+) and CD8(+) T cells (PubMed:7842483, PubMed:9000539). Also binds reversibly to natural killer (NK) cells and enhances NK cell cytotoxicity through its protease activity (PubMed:9000539, PubMed:9536127). Cleaves complement C3 (PubMed:1861080). Cleaves vimentin (By similarity). Cleaves thrombin receptor F2R/PAR1 and acts as either an agonist or an inhibitor, depending on the F2R cleavage site (PubMed:10702240, PubMed:7744748). Cleavage of F2R at '41-Arg-|-Ser-42' results in receptor activation while cleavage at '55-Phe-|-Trp-56' results in inhibition of receptor activation (PubMed:7744748). Cleaves the synovial mucin-type protein PRG4/lubricin (PubMed:32144329). Cleaves and activates IL36G which promotes expression of chemokines CXCL1 and CXLC8 in keratinocytes (PubMed:30804664). Cleaves IL33 into mature forms which have greater activity than the unprocessed form (PubMed:22307629). Cleaves coagulation factor F8 to produce a partially activated form (PubMed:18217133). Also cleaves and activates coagulation factor F10 (PubMed:8920993). Cleaves leukocyte cell surface protein SPN/CD43 to release its extracellular domain and trigger its intramembrane proteolysis by gamma-secretase, releasing the CD43 cytoplasmic tail chain (CD43-ct) which translocates to the nucleus (PubMed:18586676). Cleaves CCL5/RANTES to produce RANTES(4-68) lacking the N-terminal three amino acids which exhibits reduced chemotactic and antiviral activities (PubMed:16963625). During apoptosis, cleaves SMARCA2/BRM to produce a 160 kDa cleavage product which localizes to the cytosol (PubMed:11259672). Cleaves myelin basic protein MBP in B cell lysosomes at '224-Phe-|-Lys-225' and '248-Phe-|-Ser-249', degrading the major immunogenic MBP epitope and preventing the activation of MBP-specific autoreactive T cells (PubMed:15100291). Cleaves annexin ANXA1 and antimicrobial peptide CAMP to produce peptides which act on neutrophil N-formyl peptide receptors to enhance the release of CXCL2 (PubMed:22879591). Acts as a ligand for the N-formyl peptide receptor FPR1, enhancing phagocyte chemotaxis (PubMed:15210802). Has antibacterial activity against the Gram-negative bacteria N.gonorrhoeae and P.aeruginosa (PubMed:1937776, PubMed:2116408). Likely to act against N.gonorrhoeae by interacting with N.gonorrhoeae penA/PBP2 (PubMed:2126324). Exhibits potent antimicrobial activity against the Gram-positive bacterium L.monocytogenes (PubMed:2117044). Has antibacterial activity against the Gram-positive bacterium S.aureus and degrades S.aureus biofilms, allowing polymorphonuclear leukocytes to penetrate the biofilm and phagocytose bacteria (PubMed:2117044, PubMed:32995850). Has antibacterial activity against M.tuberculosis (PubMed:15385470). Mediates CASP4 activation induced by the Td92 surface protein of the periodontal pathogen T.denticola, causing production and secretion of IL1A and leading to pyroptosis of gingival fibroblasts (PubMed:29077095). Induces platelet aggregation which is strongly potentiated in the presence of ELANE (PubMed:25211214, PubMed:9111081) (Microbial infection) Inhibited reversibly by S.aureus serine protease inhibitors Eap, EapH1 and EapH2, impairing microbicidal activity in neutrophils",

PTPRD ↔ GPR52 IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.5 · pTM 0.39
Rationale
The real AF3 fold's topology check found the modelled A-B interface spans both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. That is impossible across an intact membrane, and it confirms the concern I could not check originally, that the large 4304 Å2 interface on a small GPCR crosses the membrane. Other evidence does not rescue the pair. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed show no prior link (known_interaction_strength=none). HPA plausibility is unknown, so there is no co-localization data to support an alternative contact. The borderline metrics (ipTM 0.5, interface PAE 9.34 Å, interface pLDDT 64.7) are the only support for the pair, and they are explained by the topologically invalid pose. The glycosylation concern is secondary. I am moving from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE for this modelled interface. A genuine extracellular or in-membrane interaction between the two proteins is not excluded.
PTM / glycosylation
Both are N-glycosylated on extracellular regions (PTPRD 4 sites, GPR52 3 sites). AF3 did not model the glycans. This is secondary to the topology violation.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association. CellPhoneDB: no match. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No known interaction.
Other subunits
IL1RAP;IL1RAPL1;SLITRK2
Follow-up (not yet executed): If the pair is still of interest, test an extracellular-domain-only PTPRD construct against GPR52 with its N-terminus and loops, or check the interaction experimentally (e.g. co-IP or proximity ligation in neurons).

ADORA1 ↔ GPR62 CONFIRMED_NOVEL VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.5 · pTM 0.61
Rationale
No prior record of this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB no match, PubMed 0 hits). Both are 7TM GPCRs with brain-elevated RNA and UniProt cell-membrane annotation, so a lateral GPCR heteromer in the same membrane is compartmentally plausible; UniProt also notes GPR62 likely heteromerizes with MTNR1B. Confidence is low because ipTM 0.5 sits exactly on the threshold, HPA shows no shared enriched cell type, GPR62 has no HPA localization data, and AF3 packing of two 7TM bundles without a bilayer is prone to non-specific interfaces.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: ADORA1 is a glycoprotein and palmitoylated lipoprotein (1 glycosylation site, 1 lipidation site); GPR62 is a glycoprotein (2 glycosylation sites). The PubMed PTM search returned 6 hits for ADORA1, none clearly about its glycosylation in the titles shown, and 0 for GPR62. Whether any of these sites lies on the modeled interface was not checked; neither function text describes a glycan-mediated binding mechanism, so this is a minor caveat rather than grounds for an artifact call.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no match (GPR62 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. Nothing indicates the pair is already known.
Other subunits
MTNR1B
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here. Inspect the AF3 model to confirm the interface is TM-helix to TM-helix in parallel orientation (not mixing cytoplasmic and extracellular residues) and that the glycosylation and palmitoylation sites are off the interface. Verify co-expression of ADORA1 and GPR62 in oligodendrocytes from full single-cell data. Test heteromerization by BRET/co-IP in co-transfected cells, with MTNR1B–GPR62 as a positive control and an unrelated GPCR as a specificity control; other_subunits lists MTNR1B as that reported GPR62 partner for comparison, not as a missing obligate subunit.

PPIA ↔ GPR63 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM medium confidence ipTM 0.5 · pTM 0.5
Rationale
The fold check shows a glycosylation or lipidation site sitting directly on the modeled PPIA–GPR63 interface. My original verdict left that unresolved, and the check now closes the gap. AF3 models bare sequence only, so any contact built around a modified residue may not match the real binding mode. This is most relevant for GPR63, an extracellular-facing GPCR with 3 UniProt glycosylation sites. It also fits my earlier concern that PPIA passed the confidence gate against 4 of 11 receptors, which points to partner-driven stickiness rather than specificity, and the ipTM of about 0.5 is only at threshold. The other evidence is unchanged: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed show no prior record, so the pair is novel but unsupported, and HPA compartments are plausible. Plausible compartments do not offset a threshold-level fold whose interface depends on a modified residue. I am therefore moving from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM, with medium confidence because I did not check whether the glycosylation site is on the GPR63 or PPIA side.
PTM / glycosylation
The real AF3 fold flagged a glycosylation or lipidation site directly on the modeled interface (ptm_only_concern). UniProt lists 3 glycosylation sites on GPR63 and 1 on PPIA. AF3 does not represent these modifications, so the modeled contact is unreliable. PPIA also binds heparan sulfate, which adds to the glycan concern.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence for PPIA and GPR63 returned 0 papers.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found (GPR63 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No prior record of this pair, so it is novel but unsupported.
Other subunits
BSG
Follow-up (not yet executed): Identify which protein carries the flagged modified residue and whether it is in the extracellular region of GPR63. Then re-fold with the glycan or modification represented, or with the site masked, and check whether the interface and ipTM hold. Also test PPIA against unrelated GPCRs as a specificity control.
